assessments.operationalization: The text proposes that an Individual is whatever scale of cybernetic goals a system can pursue. Changing the goal inventory changes the boundary by definition, so the proposal cannot be confirmed or refuted by observation.
obstacles: This is an explicit definition.
Goal-ascription and system boundary are fixed together.
assessments.rationale: The section offers a definition of an Individual drawn from its goal structure. Feedback toward a set point can be measured in particular machines and tissues, and the claim is that those goals determine the agent. That determination is stipulated. Datasets of behavior do not decide a definition.

assessments.operationalization: Body-plan disparity through time can be counted from fossils and phylogenies. A cognitive light cone is the author's goal-boundary, and expansions of morphology do not measure expansions of that boundary.
obstacles: The light cone is defined in cognitive terms that fossils do not record.
Morphological complexity is a different variable, and lineages that simplify anatomy are allowed by the claim.
assessments.rationale: The historical claim is that possible cognitive boundaries have expanded, with admitted contractions. Paleontological datasets can track bodies and sensory organs. They cannot track the volume of goals an extinct agent could pursue. Because the claim already allows contractions, almost any disparity curve is compatible with it. The trend is not a distinct empirical statement.

assessments.operationalization: A single trigger that starts eye or limb formation is a measurable developmental module. Identifying that module as memory, because learning compresses states into triggers, does not change the embryological outcome relative to an ordinary gene-regulatory hierarchy.
obstacles: Master-regulator cascades and memory engrams predict the same inductions.
No dataset records the evolutionary origin of modularity as learning.
assessments.rationale: Bioelectric or genetic triggers of eyes and hands are real experimental facts. The claim says those modules originate as memory compressing complex states into simple engrams. A hierarchical gene network without memory produces the same trigger-to-anatomy map. No observation available today separates the memory origin from that non-cognitive description.

assessments.operationalization: For the channel families that mediate touch, taste, temperature, and hearing, test bacterial and animal proteomes for homologous sequences and for a shared gating class. Homologs with the same stimulus class in bacteria would support the claim for that sense; a sense whose animal channel has no bacterial homolog, or only a distant fold with a different stimulus, would refute 'the exact same mechanism' for that sense.

candidate_datasets.name: UniProt
candidate_datasets.role: reference proteomes for presence or absence of sensory ion-channel families in bacteria and animals

candidate_datasets.name: InterPro
candidate_datasets.role: domain and family models for mechanosensitive, TRP, degenerin, and cyclic-nucleotide channel folds

obstacles: Sequence homology is a proxy for mechanism, not a recording of bacterial taste or hearing.
Some vertebrate sensory proteins, including Piezo and TMC, are weak or absent as bacterial channels.
Shared folds can gate on different stimuli.
assessments.rationale: The cited support for this sentence is comparative genomics of ion channels, and complete proteomes plus family models make that survey a standard analysis. Presence or absence can refute a strict reading for particular senses within weeks. It cannot show that bacterial cells use those proteins as touch, taste, temperature, or hearing in the animal sense. The homology half is open; the identity of sensory mechanism is only partly constrained, so the claim as stated is partially resolvable.

assessments.operationalization: Developmental trajectories and neural activity can be fit by a variational free-energy objective. Other control laws fit the same series once latent states are free, so no public time series isolates surprise minimization.
obstacles: Free-energy minimization is flexible enough to accommodate many trajectories.
Embryonic cells do not come with an observed generative model.
assessments.rationale: The claim imports the free-energy principle from nervous systems to cells in development and treats it as true of both. Expression and behavioral time series exist, and they underdetermine the objective a system is optimizing. A successful active-inference fit does not rule out simpler homeostasis. No measurement distinguishes the claim from a non-cognitive account of the same developmental path.

assessments.operationalization: Greedy infotaxis is a specific foraging algorithm. The origin of multicellularity would have to be shown to have been driven by that algorithm rather than by other benefits of staying together, and no dataset records the information-gathering objective of those ancestral cells.
obstacles: The proposal is a historical driver, not a present-day correlation.
Adhesion, feeding, and defense predict multicellularity without infotaxis.
assessments.rationale: The sentence proposes that morphological complexity and multicellularity were driven by collecting information to minimize surprise. Present-day connectivity and colony form are compatible with many selective advantages. Nothing public encodes the ancestral objective. The claim is a historical interpretation without a distinguishing observation.

assessments.operationalization: Compare the spatial scale of a response to a local stimulus in gap-junction-coupled tissue versus tissue uncoupled pharmacologically or genetically. Expansion of the responding domain while coupled, and its collapse when uncoupled, would support shared sensing; an unchanged domain would refute the physiological half of the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: GEO GSE111764
candidate_datasets.role: whole-animal planarian cell-type transcriptomes in which gap-junction gene expression can be tallied

obstacles: Expression of innexins is not functional dye coupling or shared sensation.
Common gap-junction blockers are nonspecific.
A larger responding domain can be called a larger Self or simply a larger coupled network.
assessments.rationale: Shared measurement under coupling is a measurable change in the scale of a response, and the cognitive label 'larger Self' rides on that change. Public planarian atlases show where gap-junction genes are expressed, which constrains who could be coupled and does not show stimulus sharing. Functional uncoupling experiments are published as scattered physiology, not as one imaging archive. Expression data can test a proxy and leave the binding claim only partly resolved.

assessments.operationalization: Fix a list of general and volatile anesthetics used in animals and in plants, and score each for a dye-transfer or scrape-loading reduction of gap-junction coupling. 'Most' is confirmed if a pre-specified majority reduce coupling in both kingdoms; a majority with no coupling effect, especially among plant anesthetics, would refute the generalization.

candidate_datasets.name: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology
candidate_datasets.role: curated anesthetic ligands and their molecular targets, including connexin pharmacology where it has been annotated

obstacles: Gap-junction uncoupling is not a structured field for most anesthetics.
Plant anesthesia data are much sparser than mammalian data.
A drug can close gap junctions and still act clinically through another target.
assessments.rationale: The generalization is a fraction over a definable drug list, with coupling as the assay. The Guide to Pharmacology holds the ligand list and some connexin interactions, and the coupling measurements themselves are spread through primary papers. A compilation can test the animal volatile agents that have been assayed and will miss much of the plant half. Multiple targets mean a positive uncoupling result does not show that uncoupling is how anesthesia happens, which the claim treats as support for a binding theory. The fraction is partly compilable now.

assessments.operationalization: Match named illusions or rationality failures (choice paradoxes, Weber-like biases) between a vertebrate paradigm and the same paradigm in ants and in slime molds, using choice frequencies. Shared failure modes support the scaling prediction; systematic success of the collectives on tasks where vertebrates fail, or biases with a different psychometric form, would weaken it.
obstacles: Ant and slime-mold choice data sit in individual papers, not a public trial archive.
The published overlaps cover a few paradigms, not the vertebrate illusion battery.
Similar biases can come from different mechanisms.
assessments.rationale: The prediction is comparative behavior on shared tasks, and the paper says ants and slime molds already show the failures. Those results are published measurements that a reviewer can compile, and they are not a downloadable dataset with official trial files. The overlap is a handful of paradigms, so the scope 'the same kinds of illusions' is only sampled. Mechanism differences keep the compilation suggestive. No repository is listed because none holds the choice-level data.

assessments.operationalization: Sweep a coupling or synaptic-gating parameter from isolation to full sharing and measure modularity of the resulting patterns or activity. An intermediate window with differentiated modules, flanked by fragmentation and by a homogeneous soup, would support the balance; monotone improvement with more sharing would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: BETSE
candidate_datasets.role: public tissue model in which gap-junction conductance can be swept and pattern modularity recorded

obstacles: What counts as a new Self is still a labeling choice.
The location of the intermediate window depends on how sharing is parameterized.
Empirical dose-response of coupling versus anatomical modules is not one dataset.
assessments.rationale: The non-cognitive core is a Goldilocks effect of information sharing on modularity, which a gap-junction sweep in BETSE can exhibit or fail to exhibit. That is an analysis on public code, limited to the model. Calling the successful window a Self does not add a separate measurement, and tissue dose-response data are not assembled. The model can partially test the balance and cannot establish it for organisms.

assessments.operationalization: Isolation from bioelectric signals, proliferation, and migration are measurable, and so is reversal when coupling is restored. Those outcomes are also predicted by voltage-dependent control of growth without any shrinking cognitive boundary.
obstacles: The computational-boundary wording does not change the predicted tumor phenotypes.
Reversibility of a phenotype does not measure the size of a Self.
assessments.rationale: The conclusion identifies cancer with a reversible shrink of the Self to a unicellular cognitive scale. The laboratory patterns cited for it, depolarization-linked overgrowth and hyperpolarization-linked suppression, are equally described as membrane-potential effects on cell behavior. No existing observation counts for one description and against the other. The cognitive identification is not empirically resolvable.

assessments.operationalization: Homeostasis, memory, and prediction can be ascribed to living systems after the fact. A required evolutionary sequence from loops, through delays, to networks is not a variable in phylogenetic or experimental datasets.
obstacles: The scaling path is a narrative of how agency must have been built.
Alternative orders of the same ingredients fit the same modern organisms.
assessments.rationale: The closing summary states how agents scaled up, by adding memory, anticipation, and networks to homeostatic loops under surprise minimization. Extant physiology can be described in those terms in more than one order. No dataset records the succession. The claim is a historical schema without a distinguishing test.

assessments.operationalization: Compare anatomical viability under the same mutational perturbations in lineages or models with regulative, set-point development and in matched systems without it. Smoothing is confirmed if goal-directed development yields more viable neighbor phenotypes; equal fragility would refute a ratchet that hides mutational disruption.
obstacles: No public anatomical fitness landscape is paired with a measured morphogenetic set point.
Canalization from gene-network structure produces the same smoothing.
The extra-digit anecdote is not a dataset.
assessments.rationale: Robustness of anatomy to mutation is a definable contrast between regulative and non-regulative development. The measurements that would populate that contrast, matched mutational neighborhoods of anatomy, have not been released as a dataset. Other sources of canalization predict the same smoothing, so even a future landscape would need the with-versus-without set-point arm. Existing anecdotes do not resolve the ratchet.

assessments.operationalization: In tadpoles whose only eyes are on the tail and innervated by the spinal cord, score visual learning against blinded and orthotopic-eye controls, with innervation checked by tracing. Sight without a direct brain projection would support functional adjustment; chance performance, or a hidden projection to the brain, would refute the empirical claim.
obstacles: Trial logs and axon traces are in the papers, not a repository.
Extra-ocular light sensitivity has to be excluded.
The leap from these tadpoles to brains in general is wider than the data.
assessments.rationale: Visual performance with a known, abnormal projection is a sharp test of hardwiring, and the Xenopus experiments were published with behavioral results. Those results can be read as measurements and cannot be recomputed from open trial files. Xenbase locates the phenotype literature and does not hold the learning curves. The tadpole result is partly assessable from the publications; the general claim about brains exceeds that sample.

assessments.operationalization: After a transient bioelectric perturbation in planaria, score head number across subsequent regeneration rounds in the absence of further treatment, and sequence the lines for coding changes. Permanent two-headed anatomy with no relevant sequence change would support set-point editing; reversion, or a fixed mutation, would refute the demonstrating case.
obstacles: Phenotype counts and any sequencing of the stable lines are not in a public archive.
Planarian reference genomes do not contain the edited lines.
A planarian result does not show that the strategy works as regenerative medicine in vertebrates.
assessments.rationale: Permanent anatomy across asexual generations, with the genome left unchanged, is a concrete test of the planarian example. Those worm-level outcomes and sequences were published, if at all, inside the papers, and no repository lets a third party recount heads or call variants. The regenerative-medicine recommendation is broader than that example. The demonstrating case is partly documented and not reanalyzable; the strategy claim needs data the example does not supply.

assessments.operationalization: In an ion-channel and gap-junction network, show at least two stable Vmem patterns and a transient stimulus that switches them with channel genes held fixed. Multistability under fixed parameters would support the software analogy in the model; a unique steady state, or a switch that requires changing channel expression, would refute it there. The tissue reading additionally needs a transient in vivo stimulus that permanently changes anatomy without a DNA change.

candidate_datasets.name: BETSE
candidate_datasets.role: open implementation of channel and gap-junction dynamics for testing multistability and transient switching

obstacles: A multistable model does not show that tissues occupy those attractors.
Transcriptional memory can store a new anatomical state with the DNA sequence unchanged.
No public time series records an in vivo bioelectric switch and the subsequent attractor.
assessments.rationale: The computational content, multiple attractors switched by a transient input under fixed channel parameters, is what BETSE was built to explore and can be tested by a standard parameter sweep. That resolves the circuit claim inside the model. The biological reading, that tissues actually store anatomy this way, depends on experiments whose raw physiological traces are not deposited, and transcriptional storage remains a rival. Code makes the software analogy partly resolvable and leaves the tissue claim open.

assessments.operationalization: In a basal multicellular model and in stem/somatic co-cultures, measure whether opioids increase cell-cell retention or aggregation relative to receptor-blocked controls, beyond known effects on mammalian reward circuits. A retention effect in those simple systems would support the physiological half; no effect outside nervous systems would undercut the ancient-root hypothesis.

candidate_datasets.name: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology
candidate_datasets.role: catalog of opioid receptors and ligands, which documents modern targets and not adhesion in early multicellular models

obstacles: No public co-culture or choanoflagellate dataset applies opioids and scores cell proximity.
Mammalian addiction assays do not establish an ancient cell-keeping function.
A positive adhesion effect would still be compatible with a later co-option.
assessments.rationale: The author marks this as a testable hypothesis about opioids and cell proximity in simple systems. Receptor catalogs document modern pharmacology and contain none of those aggregation measurements. A historical 'derives from' claim is only weakly tied to a future adhesion result, but the physiological prediction itself is an experiment that has not been deposited. Resolving even the weaker reading needs new assays.

assessments.operationalization: Force a defined set of electrogenic proteins and gap junctions in a unicellular species and score emergence of a stable, patterned, multi-cell body against transgenic controls; the converse is a bioelectric manipulation that disperses an existing metazoan body. Body formation only in the forced-expression arm would support the induction prediction; no change, or bodies in the controls, would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Genome
candidate_datasets.role: sequenced unicellular genomes showing which electrogenic genes are already present, not the effect of forcing them

obstacles: No public experiment forces this gene set and scores body-like morphogenesis.
Metazoan-like needs a pre-specified morphology, or any clump will count.
Dissolving a metazoan body is a separate intervention with no deposited trial.
assessments.rationale: Induction of a body-like form by a named class of genes is a direct gain-of-function test, and failure in controls would be decisive. Genomes tell which genes a unicell already has and do not contain the forcing experiment. The dissolution half is likewise untested in open data. The prediction is clear and awaits the experiment.

assessments.operationalization: In regeneration-versus-intact or regeneration-versus-wound transcriptomes, test enrichment of electrogenic genes (channels, pumps, gap-junction proteins) with a shared ortholog map from biofilms, plants, and animals. Consistent regeneration-specific enrichment across kingdoms would support the transcriptomic prediction; enrichment in only one kingdom, or only in housekeeping ion transport, would refute consistency. A second arm is whether cognitive-modulator drugs change biofilm and Physarum behavior.

candidate_datasets.name: GEO GSE88975
candidate_datasets.role: Xenopus tropicalis tail-regeneration RNA-seq across six time points, including windows the depositors associate with bioelectrical signaling

candidate_datasets.name: GEO GSE103633
candidate_datasets.role: planarian single-cell and bulk RNA-seq with regeneration time points for electrogenic-gene expression

candidate_datasets.name: GEO GSE98084
candidate_datasets.role: planarian regeneration RNA-seq under a depolarizing electrochemical perturbation, with differential expression of ion translocators

obstacles: The open series are animal, so bacterial biofilms and plants are missing from the test.
Ion-transport genes are expressed in non-regenerating tissues, so the contrast must be regeneration-specific.
Drug effects on biofilms and Physarum are not in these expression archives.
assessments.rationale: Enrichment of electrogenic genes during regeneration is a standard differential-expression analysis, and several animal regeneration series are already in GEO, including one built around electrochemical perturbation. Those series can confirm or weaken the animal limb of the consistency claim. They do not sample damaged biofilms or plant regeneration, and they contain no drug-behavior arm for biofilms or Physarum. Cross-kingdom orthology and the choice of wounded controls will determine how sharp the animal result is. The prediction is partly testable on public RNA-seq and open on the rest of its scope.

assessments.operationalization: No third-person variable would be present if a tissue had experience while deciding and absent if the same tissue only carried out the same physiological dynamics.
obstacles: Phenomenal 'something it is like' has no public measurement that separates it from the physiological description of the same events.
assessments.rationale: The hypothesis is about first-person experience in non-neural organs. Neural and physiological data can describe decision-like dynamics, and those same records remain compatible with or without proto-consciousness. Nothing in current public data supplies a confirming or refuting observation.

assessments.operationalization: Re-run the deposited evolutionary pipeline for a stated objective and compare simulated behavior with the published living builds; transfer holds if built designs show the targeted behavior and shape-scrambled builds do not.

candidate_datasets.name: reconfigurable_organisms
candidate_datasets.role: public source code for re-evolving the in silico designs and reproducing the simulation half of the pipeline

obstacles: The paper deposits computational code only; Ethovision tracks and build videos are not in an open measurement archive.
Manual construction steps mean a simulator re-run does not test the living half of the pipeline.
assessments.rationale: The in silico design loop is specified and the code was deposited for reproduction, so that half can be re-run. The claim also requires living Xenopus builds to show the predicted behaviors, and those trajectories were published as summaries and supplementary media rather than as a downloadable track dataset. Existing materials can test the computational half and only audit the biological half.

assessments.operationalization: For the reported deciliated cardiac design, compare net displacement and heading of upright versus inverted organisms in the simulator and, where tracks exist, in the living builds; the claim holds if upright heading matches the design and inversion reduces displacement in both.

candidate_datasets.name: reconfigurable_organisms
candidate_datasets.role: code to re-simulate upright and inverted designs under the paper's random actuation and score net displacement

obstacles: In vivo p-values are published, but the trial-level movement tracks are not deposited.
The quantitative claim is for at least one design, so a re-run has to recover that design rather than a new evolutionary sample.
assessments.rationale: Heading and net displacement under an inversion control are standard kinematic variables, and the simulator that produced the in silico p-values is public. The living comparison rests on published statistics from one design without an open track file, so the in vivo clause cannot be remeasured. Re-simulation can confirm or refute the computational half.

assessments.operationalization: Test whether orientation-matched designs agree with the simulation more than inverted or shape-scrambled designs; design-dependence holds if the match disappears when morphology is flipped or replaced.

candidate_datasets.name: reconfigurable_organisms
candidate_datasets.role: simulator in which orientation and shape controls can be re-run to separate design-specific locomotion from a generic bias

obstacles: A shared physical bias could make simulation and organism agree even if the evolved shape is not the cause.
The living inversion result is a published summary for a narrow set of builds.
assessments.rationale: The interpretation is tied to a concrete control: agreement should depend on orientation if the morphology, rather than a chance match, carried the behavior. That control can be repeated in the public simulator. The living data are too narrow, and shared hydrodynamics could still favor both the model and the organism, so the causal wording is only partly separable from its rivals.

assessments.operationalization: Place particles in the simulated dish and measure cluster size or particles gathered per time for motile designs versus non-motile controls; the same contrast on living builds would test the in vivo clause.

candidate_datasets.name: reconfigurable_organisms
candidate_datasets.role: voxel simulator in which particle-gathering by motile designs can be re-implemented and compared with non-motile controls

obstacles: Passive sweeping by any moving object can pile particles up without a design-specific behavior.
Living aggregation is documented in figures and video, not as deposited particle tracks.
assessments.rationale: Aggregation is measurable as particle clustering, and the simulator can be extended or re-run for the in silico half. The living half is a qualitative supplementary observation. Without non-motile controls, piled debris is also what any crawler would leave behind, so the result is only partly discriminating.

assessments.operationalization: In paired trials, score collision rate, duration of mechanical contact, and number of shared revolutions, with cilia intact versus inhibited; the claim holds if orbiting bouts are more frequent when cilia are active.

candidate_datasets.name: reconfigurable_organisms
candidate_datasets.role: soft-body simulator used for the predicted multi-body contacts, which can be re-run for collision and orbit statistics

obstacles: Orbiting can arise from generic hydrodynamic drafting once two bodies touch.
The cilia contrast is an in vivo observation without a deposited event log.
assessments.rationale: Contact duration and revolutions are countable, and the deposited simulator covers the in silico collective runs. The cilia comparison and the living orbiting bouts are qualitative and not in that repository. Hydrodynamic sticking remains a competing account of temporary orbits, so current materials test only part of the claim.

assessments.operationalization: Re-evolve locomotion under randomly phased contractile voxels and track, across generations, shape plus the fraction of passive versus contractile cells against the variance of heading or centroid velocity; derandomization holds if coherence rises under selection and stays low in unselected controls.

candidate_datasets.name: reconfigurable_organisms
candidate_datasets.role: deposited evolutionary algorithm and Voxelyze engine for re-running selection on randomly actuated soft bodies

obstacles: The 2019 VoxCad build is finicky to compile, and exact seeds are needed to match historical runs.
Coherence must be defined from the supplement; several variance metrics could be computed.
assessments.rationale: The claim is about an outcome inside a specified soft-body evolutionary simulation, and the code for that simulation is public. A small team can re-evolve populations and measure whether shape and tissue arrangement reduce the randomness of global motion relative to unselected controls. That comparison confirms or refutes the derandomization result without new biological data.

assessments.operationalization: Score whether novel, nerve-free, mixed-tissue builds maintain the designed behavior and external shape; competence-as-cause would require that outcome to survive only when a separate, pre-registered measure of cell-level cooperation is intact.
obstacles: Biophysical self-assembly predicts the same maintenance of shape and movement.
No deposited dataset records a cell-level competence variable separate from the organism-level behavior.
assessments.rationale: Maintenance of designed behavior in a novel configuration is observable and is described in the published builds. Attributing that outcome to behavioral competence and cooperation, rather than to the mechanics of adhesion and contraction, has no measurement that would come apart from those mechanics. Public materials can speak to the outcome and leave the causal wording underdetermined.

assessments.operationalization: From contraction or voltage traces in built organisms, compute phase lag among cardiac regions; spontaneous coordination holds if phase-locking exceeds a shuffle of independent cells and was not imposed by the construction protocol.
obstacles: The data release covers simulation code, not cardiomyocyte timing traces.
Supplementary video, where present, is an illustration rather than a sample of phase measurements.
assessments.rationale: Phase-matched contraction is a standard physiological measurement and would be distinguishable from independent twitching. The paper reports the coordination and deposits the simulator, which assumes actuation rather than recording it. No public trace archive supports a reanalysis, so the test needs the original timing data or a new recording.

assessments.operationalization: After a standardized laceration, measure wound width over time against uninjured shape landmarks; self-repair holds if the gap closes and the external configuration returns, beyond passive recoil.
obstacles: The support is a supplementary example, not a deposited series with sample size and controls.
Tissue recoil and wound contraction can close a gap without a regulated repair response.
assessments.rationale: Wound closure and shape maintenance are measurable. The published support is an illustrative supplementary figure, and re-inspecting that figure is not a test of rates, sample size, or passive recoil. A quantitative decision needs the original time series or a new assay.

assessments.operationalization: Re-evaluate pass-1 and pass-2 designs in the deposited simulator and compute the fraction of time steps with ground contact; the numerical claim holds if pass 2 is near 93.3 percent and pass 1 near 52.7 percent under the published evaluation window.

candidate_datasets.name: reconfigurable_organisms
candidate_datasets.role: pass-1 and pass-2 evolutionary experiments whose ground-contact time can be recomputed in Voxelyze

obstacles: Matching the published percentages requires the same evaluation window and random seeds described in the supplement.
Living ground-contact was not deposited as a paired percentage, so the match to organisms is carried by the simulation contrast.
assessments.rationale: The quantitative content is a pair of ground-contact fractions from two specified simulation passes, and the code for those passes is public. Recomputing contact time confirms or refutes the 93.3 versus 52.7 percent contrast with a standard geometric measurement. The link to living gaits is the reason the second pass was defined, and it is checked by whether that pass stays on the substrate as the paper's living builds do.

assessments.operationalization: Shape animal-cap aggregates with concavities of graded width and record whether each gap remains after a fixed culture interval; the size threshold holds if gaps at or above 100 micrometers persist and smaller gaps close.
obstacles: The result is described as preliminary work in a supplement figure, without a deposited morphometry table.
Testing it again requires new microsurgical aggregates.
assessments.rationale: Concavity width and persistence are direct morphometric variables with a clear threshold. The published support is a preliminary supplementary figure, not an open table of widths and outcomes. Confirming or refuting the 100 micrometer cutoff requires those measurements or a new build series.

assessments.operationalization: A census of cognitive systems would need a part to count as an agent by a criterion that could fail; under the claim's usage, any functional part can be counted as an agent.
obstacles: 'Agent in important ways' can be applied to whatever parts a system has, so no catalog of organisms yields a refuting case.
assessments.rationale: Biological cognitive systems are structurally made of parts, which is true by anatomy and does not need a dataset. Calling those parts agents, and concluding there is no indivisible cognitive being, does not add an observation that would distinguish the claim from a non-agential parts list. The universal wording is fixed by the definition in use.

assessments.operationalization: Compare time-to-criterion or savings after regeneration between animals trained before decapitation and naive regenerates; persistence holds if trained animals relearn faster after a new brain is built, with motility equated.
obstacles: Raw tracking logs from the automated assay were not deposited.
Residual body tissue, sensitization, and one-tailed tests can mimic savings without a memory stored outside the original brain.
Classical manual studies and the 2013 familiarization assay do not cover the same tasks.
assessments.rationale: Memory here has a workable behavioral meaning: faster return to criterion after training, measured again after the head regenerates. Published tables from the automated familiarization study and older training papers contain summary counts, scattered across journals rather than in one archive. Those summaries can be re-read for effect direction, and they leave the main confounds and the raw latencies unchecked.

assessments.operationalization: In the light-mediated learning assay, compare choice performance of tadpoles with ectopic tail eyes and native eyes removed against blind and normal-eyed animals; visual learning holds if only animals with a functional eye-brain path exceed chance.
obstacles: Trial-level choice logs are in the papers' summaries, not a public repository.
Both positive reports come from the same group, so an independent replicate is not in the open record.
assessments.rationale: The learning assay and the blind and innervated controls map onto choice rates that the 2013 and 2017 papers publish for this Xenopus preparation. Those measurements cover the stated scope and can be checked for whether tail-eye animals outperform eyeless controls. Without deposited trial logs, a new analyst cannot recompute the statistics from raw choices.

assessments.operationalization: On one pre-registered cognitive or neural trait, test whether sister lineages differ by jumps that are large relative to within-lineage variation and short relative to individual lifespan; a continuum holds if changes are graded on that trait.
obstacles: Neuron counts, brain size, and learning scores are different operationalizations and need not agree.
A graded proxy can hide a qualitative change in a capacity the proxy does not measure.
'Have not been shown' is a claim about the literature as well as about the organisms.
assessments.rationale: Comparative compilations of brain size, neuron number, and learning scores exist as scattered published tables and can be tested for saltations versus grades on those proxies. No single public matrix covers cognition across the claim's full range of organisms, and competing proxies answer differently. The result can pressure a strong binary reading and cannot settle cognitive capacity as such.

assessments.operationalization: Model comparison can rank which description predicts and controls a system most efficiently, and under this claim the winner is the correct agency level by definition.
obstacles: Every outcome of a predictive comparison is compatible with the claim, because the claim stipulates that the best-controlling model is the right level of agency.
assessments.rationale: The statement is a rule for attributing agency: use whichever model gives the most efficient prediction and control. Experiments can rank models, and the ranking cannot come out against the rule, because the rule defines the preferred level as the winner. That is a methodological stipulation rather than a result public data could refute.

assessments.operationalization: On published GRN models, pair a cue with an outcome-producing stimulus and test whether the cue later changes the response relative to unpaired controls; associative learning, pattern completion, or generalization holds if the paired network meets that criterion and a shuffled network does not.

candidate_datasets.name: Cell Collective
candidate_datasets.role: public Boolean gene-regulatory models, including the networks used in the cited memory surveys

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: public ODE models of biological pathways that can be re-simulated for stimulus-pairing tests

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: code for a follow-up memory screen of continuous BioModels networks

obstacles: Code for the 2021 Boolean memory screen was withheld, so the exact published runs cannot be replayed.
Associative learning, pattern completion, and generalization are defined differently across the cited papers.
assessments.rationale: The models themselves are public, in Cell Collective and BioModels, and a later ODE analysis has open code, so a defined pairing protocol can be re-run. The flagship Boolean analysis did not release its code, and the cited papers do not share one decision rule. A new screen can test learning capacity in the published models and will not automatically reproduce each cited result.

assessments.operationalization: Goals, associative memory, and credit assignment can be measured in a particular system, but finding them would illustrate this definition of a Self rather than test it.
obstacles: The statement stipulates the hallmarks of a Self, so empirical cases are examples of the definition.
assessments.rationale: The text presents these three capacities as the basic hallmarks TAME will use. A system that shows them fits the definition, and a system that lacks them falls outside it. Public data can hunt for the capacities and cannot confirm or refute the stipulation that they are what a Self is.

assessments.operationalization: The spatial and temporal reach of a measured setpoint can be plotted, and the claim then calls that plot the boundary of the Self.
obstacles: Once goal scale is measured, identifying it with the boundary of the Self is true by the proposed diagram, with no rival outcome.
assessments.rationale: Spatiotemporal scale of a homeostatic target is something an experiment could estimate for a given system. The claim uses that scale as the delineation of the Self, which is the framework's classification rule. Any measured scale is compatible with the rule, so the statement does not have a separate empirical consequence.

assessments.operationalization: Impose a local deviation from a measured setpoint, record whether distant modules change their activity, and block the candidate signal; binding holds if remote action reduces the original error and fails when the signal is blocked.
obstacles: Ordinary physiological coupling spreads signals without binding modules into one homeostatic individual.
Setpoint error, remote recruitment, and error reduction are rarely measured together outside a few injury preparations.
Published injury-spread results cover a small slice of multicellular organisms.
assessments.rationale: Long-range injury signals and compensatory responses are reported in a handful of regeneration papers, as summaries rather than a shared dataset. Those records can show that a wound changes distant tissue. They do not contain the joint measurement of setpoint error, recruitment, and error reduction that would separate one homeostatic loop from ordinary coupling.

assessments.operationalization: Date gene families used in physiological and morphogenetic control against the origin of nervous systems and 3D behavioral circuits; the sequential claim is supported only as a proxy if those families are older and later co-opted into neural control.

candidate_datasets.name: OrthoDB
candidate_datasets.role: phyletic profiles of gene families to see which physiological and morphogenetic regulators predate nervous systems

candidate_datasets.name: Ensembl
candidate_datasets.role: annotated metazoan genomes for presence of the same families in aneural and neural lineages

candidate_datasets.name: TimeTree
candidate_datasets.role: clade divergence times for ordering those gene origins against the origin of nervous systems

obstacles: Shared genes are compatible with later co-option and do not show that behavioral strategies are variants of older ones.
Problem-solving in metabolic or morphogenetic space is not a variable in these databases.
assessments.rationale: Public orthology and divergence-time resources can test whether components of physiological and morphogenetic control are older than nervous systems. That is a proxy for the proposed timeline. The claim that 3D behavioral problem-solving is the same strategy pivoted into a new space is not distinguished by gene age alone.

assessments.operationalization: Reanalyze GSE98084 for the fraction of transcripts that change in barium-adapted heads versus wild-type heads, and compare that count with the paper's survival and regeneration tallies in BaCl2; the transcriptional clause holds if only a small fraction of the transcriptome moves.

candidate_datasets.name: Gene Expression Omnibus
candidate_datasets.role: series GSE98084, public RNA-seq of barium-adapted versus wild-type Dugesia japonica heads, for recounting differentially expressed transcripts

obstacles: Two biological replicates limit how firmly 'relatively few genes' can be reestimated.
Head loss and later barium insensitivity are phenotype counts in the paper, not in the expression series.
Differential expression does not show that the cells searched transcriptional space for a solution evolution had not already produced.
assessments.rationale: The expression half is in a public RNA-seq series and can be reanalyzed with a standard differential-expression pipeline. Phenotype claims, that heads are lost and the regenerated heads are barium-insensitive, sit in the paper's counts with no separate deposited assay table. The navigational reading of those gene changes is not separated by the expression matrix from a narrower physiological compensation.

assessments.operationalization: Track craniofacial organ positions from scrambled tadpole arrangements through metamorphosis and test whether endpoints cluster on the normal frog-face coordinates even when the paths are abnormal or overshoot.
obstacles: Landmark time series are published as paper figures and summaries, not as a deposited coordinate table.
Mechanical packing in the head could funnel organs toward the same endpoints.
assessments.rationale: Endpoint position versus path shape is a direct test, and the Xenopus craniofacial papers report morphometrics for this preparation, including abnormal paths and overshoot. Those measurements are scattered in journal figures rather than an open coordinate file. They can support the setpoint reading for this species and leave mechanical funneling as a live alternative.

assessments.operationalization: Pair the location of an antler wound in one year with tine positions after shedding, against unwounded antlers; a rewritable target holds if ectopic tines recur at the wound site and can be changed by a later injury.
obstacles: The observations are case reports and older natural-history figures, not a coordinate database.
Local scar, pedicle damage, or broken bone can place a tine without a rewritten morphological setpoint.
Few species and few animals are described quantitatively.
assessments.rationale: Location-specific ectopic tines in later antler cycles are described in published case literature and could be compiled for a weak spatial test. There is no public table of wound coordinates, subsequent tines, and controls. Scar and structural damage remain competing accounts, so existing reports can illustrate the pattern and cannot settle the memory interpretation.

assessments.operationalization: Count heads, and compare head and brain landmarks to reference species, after gap-junction or ion-channel perturbation versus vehicle; the claim holds if one, two, and zero heads, and non-native head shapes, occur above the vehicle rate.

candidate_datasets.name: Planform
candidate_datasets.role: curated database of published planarian regeneration experiments, including drug treatments and organ-level morphologies

obstacles: Most quantitative series come from one laboratory, and raw images are not in a measurement archive.
Planform encodes published outcomes and may omit landmark-level shapes from later papers.
Toxicity can change head number unless vehicle and washout controls are carried along.
assessments.rationale: Head number and morphometric distance to reference species are standard variables, and several papers publish counts for gap-junction and channel perturbations in regenerating planaria. Planform compiles literature experiments of this kind, while the underlying images and landmarks remain in the papers. The phenotypic claim can be audited for the reported species and manipulations, short of an independent raw-data reanalysis.

assessments.operationalization: Cut transiently treated two-headed or zero-headed worms with no further drug and score head number in successive regenerates, alongside a wild-type sequence or drug-residue assay; persistence holds if abnormal head number continues after the drug is gone and the genome matches wild type.

candidate_datasets.name: Planform
candidate_datasets.role: encoded published regeneration outcomes, including head number after pharmacological treatments, for experiments that were curated

obstacles: Penetrance tables are in the papers, not as animal-level files.
Residual drug or a selected genetic variant can mimic a permanent physiological state.
Wild-type genome is argued from induction and reset experiments more often than from deposited sequence of the altered lines.
assessments.rationale: Head counts across amputation rounds with no further treatment are published for the octanol and related protocols. Planform may contain the curated head-number outcomes; it does not replace the raw counts. Persistence can be checked at the level of those published penetrances, and the genetic-wild-type clause stays weakly tested without sequence of the same lines.

assessments.operationalization: Apply a transient bioelectric perturbation, remove it, and test whether a new regenerative target persists across further amputations; the memory reading holds if the new target remains after tissue composition and channel expression have returned to the original state.

candidate_datasets.name: Planform
candidate_datasets.role: published planarian drug and regeneration records that capture stable changes in head number after treatment

obstacles: A lasting change in cell composition or channel expression is a non-memory account of the same regenerative outcome.
Data are concentrated in planaria, while the claim says the mechanism is conserved across regenerating animals.
The optogenetic analogy is not a separate measurement.
assessments.rationale: A regenerative target that outlasts a transient gap-junction or channel treatment is documented for planaria in published penetrance data and, where curated, in Planform. Calling that change a false pattern memory, and a conserved mechanism across animals, goes beyond those head-number records. Tissue state and expression can carry the same persistence, and other taxa are thinly covered.

assessments.operationalization: In polyploid newt larvae, count cells per tubule cross-section, cell size, and lumen diameter; the anatomical claim holds if larger cells yield fewer cells per cross-section and the largest cells form a one-cell lumen of normal size.
obstacles: The measurements are in 1945 plates and counts, not a digital archive.
Cytoskeletal bending versus cell-cell signaling was inferred from the geometry, not measured with molecular markers.
The sample is one amphibian under classical polyploidy methods.
assessments.rationale: Cell number, cell size, and lumen size are the variables Fankhauser published for newt tubules, including the single-cell case. Those counts can be compiled from the papers and cannot be remeasured from a public image set. The further claim that distinct molecular mechanisms are deployed for the same lumen is an interpretation of the geometry rather than a result in the old plates.

assessments.operationalization: Decode amputation level and injury type from images of the uninjured contralateral limb at 30 seconds, against sham and dye-only controls; readout holds if classification accuracy exceeds chance at that latency.
obstacles: The published assay soaks tissue in voltage dye for about 30 minutes and reports depolarization by about one hour, so the 30-second clause is not in those summaries.
Images and animal-level measurements were not deposited.
DiBAC fluorescence is not a pure membrane-voltage measurement, and the mirror-neuron wording is not a variable in the assay.
assessments.rationale: The 2018 Xenopus study publishes correlations between stump geometry and the spatial extent of contralateral dye signal, which can be checked as a somatotopic association. The imaging window in that paper is dye incubation and a response on the order of an hour, and the images are not in a repository. The 30-second latency and the mirror-neuron description cannot be resolved from the published summaries.

assessments.operationalization: Test enrichment between morphogenesis genes and learning or memory genes after removing ion channels, connexins, and neurotransmitter machinery, using a degree-matched null; also test whether learning and memory genes are enriched in cancer, regeneration, and embryogenesis gene sets.

candidate_datasets.name: Gene Ontology
candidate_datasets.role: public gene annotations for morphogenesis, learning, memory, regeneration, and embryonic development, with evidence codes for an overlap test

candidate_datasets.name: GWAS Catalog
candidate_datasets.role: public genetic-association results for asking whether learning and memory genes recur in studies of other traits, including disease

obstacles: GO annotations are biased toward human, mouse, and heavily studied genes.
Regeneration genetics is largely RNAi and mutant screens, which are less completely captured by GO and the GWAS Catalog than cancer is.
assessments.rationale: Both clauses are gene-set comparisons, and the annotations and association catalogs needed for them are public and standard to analyze in days. Removing the already-shared channel, connexin, and transmitter genes is a pre-registered way to test specificity, and a null result would refute excess overlap. Coverage is weaker for regeneration screens and for non-mammalian animals than for human learning and development genes, which limits scope rather than blocking the test.

assessments.operationalization: Deliver a nutrient, endorphin, or shock contingency contingent on an anatomical or expression state, against a yoked non-contingent control; trainability holds if only the contingent group moves toward the rewarded morphology.
obstacles: No public experiment pairs contingent reward or punishment with a morphological endpoint.
Later discussions and proposed reinforcement protocols have not released such an outcome dataset.
assessments.rationale: A reinforcement test with yoked controls would cleanly confirm or refute trainability of a morphological outcome. The source paper marks the experiment as not yet done, and public follow-up through 2026 is proposal and framework rather than a deposited training result. The necessary measurements are still to be collected.

assessments.operationalization: Simulate a transient voltage pulse with published channel and connexin gating and test for two stable voltages or coupling states; dynamical memory holds if the post-pulse state remains after the pulse and changes later input-output behavior with the same hardware.

candidate_datasets.name: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology
candidate_datasets.role: curated gating and ligand data for voltage-gated channels and connexins used to parameterize a memory simulation

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: published differential-equation models of excitable membranes and gap-junction coupling that can be re-integrated

obstacles: Most kinetic parameters come from neurons or heterologous cells, not the non-neural tissues in the claim.
A persistent voltage in real tissue can be transcriptional or ultrastructural rather than a dynamical-system memory of the same channels.
assessments.rationale: Voltage-gated channel and connexin kinetics are public, and published ODE models can be re-run to see whether a transient voltage leaves a stable state. That tests the biophysical implication in models. It does not cover non-neural tissues generally, and tissue experiments that would separate dynamical memory from a changed proteome are not in one open dataset.

assessments.operationalization: Tracer studies can show that material crossing a gap junction carries no origin label, and the same records are what a larger Self and ordinary shared cytoplasm both predict.
obstacles: Loss of a diffusion barrier and formation of a larger Self predict the same coupling, coordination, and shared signals.
assessments.rationale: Gap junctions pass small molecules without tagging the sender, which follows from the structure of the pore and is already standard physiology. The further claim that this erasure creates a larger Self working toward common goals uses those same coupling facts. No additional observation would favor the Self wording over shared signals through open junctions.

assessments.operationalization: Compare connexin expression, and where available dye-coupling, between transformed and matched normal tissue, and between carcinogen-exposed and control cells; the physiological clause holds if coupling falls as transformation proceeds.

candidate_datasets.name: Genomic Data Commons
candidate_datasets.role: TCGA and related tumor expression for connexin genes across cancers, a proxy for gap-junction status

candidate_datasets.name: Gene Expression Omnibus
candidate_datasets.role: public expression series after carcinogen exposure or oncogene activation that include gap-junction transcripts

obstacles: Transcript abundance is not gap-junction closure or dye coupling.
Connexin loss is common in tumors and is neither necessary nor sufficient for transformation.
A shrinking computational Self is not a separate variable from loss of coupling and altered growth.
assessments.rationale: Public tumor and exposure expression archives can test whether connexin genes fall with transformation, which is the measurable core of the gap-junction clause. Functional closure is only in scattered dye-transfer papers. The reading that cancer is a reversion to unicellular selves with smaller computational boundaries is not distinguished by those expression patterns from loss of coupling plus proliferation.

assessments.operationalization: Score melanocyte conversion in wild-type Xenopus after a bioelectric perturbation, and score tumor-like structures in p53 or KRAS backgrounds with and without a normalizing voltage manipulation; override holds if incidence moves in the predicted direction on a wild-type genome.
obstacles: Counts are in the Xenopus papers, not a deposited animal-level table.
The readouts are embryo pigment and tumor-like foci, a narrow stand-in for metastatic melanoma and clinical reversion.
The positive series are from one laboratory.
assessments.rationale: Incidence of the reported Xenopus phenotypes under voltage manipulation, with and without oncogenes, is published with controls and covers the claim's stated embryo scope. Those numbers can be audited and cannot be recomputed from raw images, because no image or count archive was released. The jump from these foci to metastatic melanoma in general is outside what the measurements contain.

assessments.operationalization: Map ion-channel, connexin, and innexin families onto aneural animals and their unicellular relatives versus the origin of neurons; precedence of the genes holds if the families are present before nervous systems, which still leaves their developmental use untested.

candidate_datasets.name: OrthoDB
candidate_datasets.role: ortholog presence of bioelectric gene families in sponges, placozoans, ctenophores, and choanoflagellates

candidate_datasets.name: Ensembl
candidate_datasets.role: annotated genomes for the same early-branching animals and for animals with nervous systems

obstacles: Gene presence in a sponge or placozoan does not show that the genes were used to place the body in morphospace.
Channels have many functions besides positional control, so their age is compatible with other histories.
assessments.rationale: Public genomes can show that many bioelectric gene families occur in animals without neurons and in close unicellular relatives, which bears on which hardware came first. The claim also says evolution used analog bioelectric dynamics to position body configuration before neural spiking. That use is not a column in the genome matrices, so gene age is only a partial test.

assessments.operationalization: Build a presence-absence matrix of voltage- and ligand-gated channel families across unicellular eukaryotes and early metazoans and test whether context-sensitive families originate at the metazoan node, alongside gains in body-plan complexity.

candidate_datasets.name: OrthoDB
candidate_datasets.role: phyletic profiles for ion-channel families across unicellular eukaryotes and early animals

candidate_datasets.name: UniProt
candidate_datasets.role: protein sequences and functional notes for classifying channels as voltage- or ligand-gated

candidate_datasets.name: InterPro
candidate_datasets.role: domain annotations used to detect channel families in genomes that lack detailed physiology

obstacles: Domain presence is an imperfect stand-in for context-sensitive gating.
Channel gains at the origin of animals coincide with many other novelties, so a correlation does not isolate body-plan complexity.
The further continuum from excitability through somatic patterning to cognition is not in these matrices.
assessments.rationale: Channel-family presence across choanoflagellates, sponges, ctenophores, and cnidarians can be rebuilt from public orthology and domain databases with a standard phylogenetic presence-absence analysis. That tests whether context-sensitive families appear with metazoan complexity, within the limits of domain-based classification. It does not test the claimed continuum onward to cognition.

assessments.operationalization: Score eye markers and lens or retinal histology in gut, spinal cord, and posterior tissue after misexpression of one ion channel, and run Pax6 at the same sites; the contrast holds if the channel induces complete eyes where Pax6 does not.
obstacles: Histology and induction rates are in the papers, not a public image archive.
The Pax6 comparison comes from a separate vertebrate study, so sites and criteria are not matched in one dataset.
'Complete eye' has been scored with markers and anatomy of varying stringency.
assessments.rationale: Induction frequency and histological completeness are measurable, and the channel and Pax6 papers publish those observations for ectopic sites. They are not deposited as reanalyzable images, and the Pax6 insufficiency claim rests on a different experimental series. Existing write-ups can partially audit the contrast and cannot re-score the sections.

assessments.operationalization: Test whether mutations in electrogenic genes produce coordinated, multi-site anatomical changes, using zebrafish genotype-phenotype records, and separately test whether KCNH8 or a connexin is causal in the fish fin shift rather than merely differentially expressed.

candidate_datasets.name: ZFIN
candidate_datasets.role: zebrafish genotype-phenotype records for electrogenic mutants, including fin morphologies, as a partial test that such mutations can reshape anatomy

obstacles: The cited fish-fin result identifies KCNH8 and a connexin in a transcriptome of a developing ornament, which is expression rather than a demonstrated causal mutation.
A raw RNA-seq accession for that study was not confirmed here, so the expression list cannot be assumed reanalyzable from a named archive.
Zebrafish fin mutants do not establish the evolutionary swap of channels in the swordtail case.
assessments.rationale: Zebrafish phenotype databases record anatomical effects of mutations in some potassium-channel genes, which can test the narrower claim that electrogenic mutations can change morphology in a coordinated way. The evolutionary example is a candidate-gene expression result during fin outgrowth, and differential expression does not show that a mutation caused the species difference. Public data therefore cover a related genetic possibility and leave the historical case weakly tested.

assessments.operationalization: In an evolutionary simulation, compare the fitness effect and fixation of a morphology-displacing mutation with and without a module that corrects anatomy toward a target; shielding holds if the same mutation is more nearly neutral when correction is present.
obstacles: No deposited simulation was found that already compares fitness landscapes with and without morphogenetic correction.
Comparative mutational-robustness data for regulative versus mosaic developers are too sparse to stand in for that contrast.
assessments.rationale: The prediction has a clear computational contrast: the same disruptive mutation should be less visible to selection when competent modules correct anatomy. That run was not located as public code or output, and organismal datasets do not contain the paired with-versus-without comparison. Resolving the claim needs that simulation or a new comparative measurement.

assessments.operationalization: Repair of injury and correction of a mutational displacement use the same homeostasis measurements, so either selective history remains compatible with the same present-day data.
obstacles: A mechanism that corrects both wounds and mutational deviations does not record which of those roles was the primary historical reason.
assessments.rationale: Anatomical homeostasis can be shown to reduce error after cuts and after experimental displacements, and both results fit a system shaped by injury, by mutation, or by both. The claim is about the primary evolutionary reason. Present physiological and phylogenetic records do not separate that historical purpose from the other.

assessments.operationalization: No public measurement would be positive if a morphogenetic or transcriptional system had a minimal degree of consciousness and negative if it only regulated those variables.
obstacles: Degree of consciousness, as first-person experience, is not separated by any dataset from competent regulation in the same state space.
assessments.rationale: The statement infers a minimal degree of consciousness for systems whose perception and action are in morphogenetic or transcriptional spaces. Regulation, goal-like setpoints, and transcriptional change are measurable, and those measurements are exactly what a non-conscious account of the same systems also predicts. No existing dataset draws the distinction.

assessments.operationalization: Compare anesthetic potency at connexins with potency at primary targets such as GABA-A receptors, and test whether selective gap-junction blockers stop organism-level behavior in plants, Hydra, and animals while cell viability remains.

candidate_datasets.name: IUPHAR/BPS Guide to Pharmacology
candidate_datasets.role: curated target and ligand records for anesthetics, connexins, and the primary neural receptors

candidate_datasets.name: ChEMBL
candidate_datasets.role: public bioactivity values for asking whether general anesthetics block gap junctions at concentrations that anesthetize

obstacles: Many anesthetics act on synaptic receptors at concentrations below those reported for connexin block.
Behavioral arrest in plants and Hydra is in a few papers, not in these pharmacology databases.
Disappearance of a higher-level Self is not a variable separate from loss of coordinated behavior.
assessments.rationale: Pharmacology databases can test whether general anesthetics inhibit connexins, and at what concentration relative to their main targets. That addresses the gap-junction-blocker clause and can fail it for agents whose clinical action is elsewhere. Loss of a higher-level Self, and anesthesia by gap-junction block from plants to humans, is only partly represented by those ligand tables.

assessments.operationalization: After a brief octanol exposure, classify regenerated Girardia head shape against reference species at the end of regeneration and again weeks later; the morphological claim holds if non-native shapes are enriched early and then return to the species-typical shape.

candidate_datasets.name: Planform
candidate_datasets.role: curated planarian regeneration morphologies, useful for drug-induced head outcomes that were encoded from the literature

obstacles: Landmark coordinates and time courses live in the 2015 paper and its supplement, not as a confirmed open morphometric file.
Planform may store categorical outcomes rather than the remodeling trajectory.
The parallel with anesthesia is an interpretation and is not tested by head shape.
assessments.rationale: Species-likeness scores over time are a direct test, and the octanol study publishes morphometrics and a later return to Girardia shape for this protocol. Planform can hold curated morphology outcomes and does not replace those landmarks. The shape time course can be audited from the paper, and the analogy to loss and return of a Self under anesthesia is not an additional empirical result in the data.

assessments.operationalization: Re-simulate the 35 BioModels ODE pathways with the published UCS/CS/response assays and count, for each model, which of the five memory labels appear under the paper's up- and down-regulation criteria. Finding several of those labels across the set would confirm the claim; finding only one label, or none, would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: public ODE models of the surveyed gene, protein and metabolic pathways

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: MATLAB implementation of the memory test suite used on those models

obstacles: Memory labels depend on the paper's twofold up-regulation and half down-regulation cutoffs.
The repository is an unrefactored MATLAB snapshot and does not include the converted model files.
assessments.rationale: The five memory assays and the regulation thresholds are specified in the methods, the pathway models are in BioModels, and the authors' MATLAB suite is public, so re-running the survey is analysis rather than new research. The job is large and cluster-oriented, and the code is described as temporary, but a small team could rerun the suite. Agreement on which memory types occur would settle the claim as stated about these models.

assessments.operationalization: Recompute memory-type prevalence, no-memory rates and cross-type correlations for the 35 biological models and for random ODE networks matched on the stated size and centrality measures. A higher biological prevalence on most types, with fewer no-memory cases and stronger correlations, would support the contrast; a matched or reversed pattern would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: curated biological pathway ODEs used as the biological arm of the comparison

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: code that builds the matched random gene-circuit ODEs and scores memory

obstacles: Random networks use a synthetic gene-circuit equation, while the biological set mixes protein and genetic models.
BioModels is a publication-biased sample, so enrichment need not mean selection for trainability.
assessments.rationale: The prevalence contrast can be recomputed from public models and code. It does not cleanly show that generic network dynamics are uninvolved, because the null model is a different dynamical family matched only on a few structural summaries. The comparison tests a restricted version of the claim and leaves the evolutionary reading confounded.

assessments.operationalization: In the published pathway ODEs, test whether a stimulation schedule found by the memory search changes a designated response without editing parameters or edges, and compare that in silico control with the absence of any public study in which such a schedule replaces a gene-therapy outcome. In-model control without rewiring would support only the computational half; a therapeutic alternative would require a failed or successful head-to-head that does not yet exist.

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: in silico stimulation schedules that alter pathway responses without rewiring

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: pathway models on which those schedules can be re-tested

obstacles: No public dataset compares behaviour-shaping of a pathway with genomic editing on a clinical or cellular endpoint.
A hedged 'potential alternative' is compatible with both success and failure of future trials.
assessments.rationale: The models and code can show that stimulation changes a simulated response without rewiring, which is only a proxy for the biomedical claim. Nothing public tests whether that strategy substitutes for gene therapy against pharmacoresistance or sensitization in cells or patients. The claim as a therapeutic proposal stays only partly testable.

assessments.operationalization: The sentence stipulates a definition of memory rather than a measurable regularity. No observation would confirm or refute the decision to use that definition.
obstacles: A stipulated definition has no confirming or refuting measurement.
assessments.rationale: The claim states how the authors use the word memory inside their framework. Later assays apply that wording, but this statement itself cannot come out true or false from data. It is definitional.

assessments.operationalization: Rerun the memory screen and count how many of the 35 models lack every memory type, then record the node counts of those exceptions and of a broader set of BioModels with fewer than four nodes. All-but-four, with three of the four below four nodes, would confirm the census; memory in most sub-four-node models, or a different exception count, would refute the size suggestion.

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: the surveyed pathways and other small ODE models for a size check

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: memory screen whose exception count can be recomputed

obstacles: Three small exceptions do not separate 'cannot have memory' from 'this assay missed it'.
The surveyed set was not built as a systematic sweep of network size.
assessments.rationale: The exception count among the 35 models is a direct rerun. The further claim that very small networks cannot or almost never have memory is an extrapolation from three cases and is not covered by a size-balanced public sample. Only the census half is well powered.

assessments.operationalization: For each of the 35 models, pair a memory-count with mean node number, edge number, degree and hubness, and test rank correlations. Significant associations would refute the null result; consistently non-significant correlations would reproduce it, without showing that no structural feature matters.

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: SBML structure from which node, edge, degree and hubness statistics can be computed

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: memory scores and saved matrices to correlate with those statistics

obstacles: Thirty-five models give low power, so a non-significant correlation is a weak null.
Hubness and degree definitions, and multiple testing across memory types, are easy to vary.
assessments.rationale: Topology is in the SBML files and memory scores can be recomputed, so the correlation test is straightforward. A failure to find a significant correlation in this small curated set does not show that no network property indicates memory. The test is informative only inside the original sample and statistic.

assessments.operationalization: Classify feedback loops and hysteresis in the BioModels SBML graphs, then compare memory prevalence in models with and without those loops. Memory enriched in loop-containing models, plus at least some memory in models that lack them, would support the hedged claim; memory absent outside loops, or no enrichment, would count against it.

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: reaction graphs in which feedback and cycles can be enumerated

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: memory labels to cross-tabulate with loop structure

obstacles: Feedback is common in published pathway models, so co-occurrence is a weak causal test.
'May be conducive' and 'one way of many' are hard to refute with a binary loop count.
assessments.rationale: Loop structure and memory labels are both recoverable from public models and code. The wording is permissive, and the MAPK example does not isolate feedback from other dynamics. The analysis can check co-occurrence, not that loops are a cause or that they are dispensable in general.

assessments.operationalization: Rerun associative and other memory assays while logging whether rate parameters and the reaction graph stay fixed, and test whether the response remains altered after the clamp is released. Persistent change with an unchanged model file would confirm dynamical memory; memory that appears only after an edit to parameters or edges would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: stimulation code that clamps expression without rewriting reactions

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: original ODE definitions against which structural edits can be checked

obstacles: A temporary clamp is an external drive, which a rival description can treat as a transient parameter change.
assessments.rationale: The methods fix the ODE system and apply stimuli by clamping a variable, then score persistence after release. Public code and the original models make that contrast re-runnable. If the stored response survives with the same equations, the claim about these pathway models is confirmed or refuted directly.

assessments.operationalization: Repeat the memory screen at stimulus amplitudes of 10, 50 and 100 times baseline and compare memory counts per model with the baseline screen. Most models keeping the same count, about 10 percent losing memories, and some gaining memories at weaker stimuli, would confirm the claim; widespread loss at higher amplitudes would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: stimulus-scaling and memory-evaluation scripts

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: pathway ODEs on which the amplitude sweep is defined

obstacles: The main methods text specifies clamping to each variable's observed max and min, so the 10x, 50x and 100x factors need to be matched in the code or supplement.
The full combinatorial screen at three amplitudes is computationally heavy.
assessments.rationale: The decision rule is a numerical comparison of memory counts across three stated amplitudes, and both the models and the evaluation code are public. Some ambiguity remains about how 'baseline' is scaled in the MATLAB files versus the prose. That is a finite reimplementation check, not a missing experiment.

assessments.operationalization: Rerun the memory assays with the repository's stochastic perturbation and compare per-type memory counts with the deterministic runs. Retention in about 83 percent of models and a roughly 20 percent rise, largest for associative memory, would reproduce the numerical claim; a drop, or a rise concentrated in another memory type, would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: noise-enabled memory evaluator for the ODE pathways

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: deterministic pathway models to which the noise is added

obstacles: One added-noise scheme is not biological noise in cells, so the therapeutic suggestion is not identified.
The 20 percent average depends on how memory phenotypes are pooled.
assessments.rationale: A public noise script can recheck the 83 percent retention and the 20 percent increase inside this simulation. The claim also treats that stochasticity as evidence about biological noise and trainability, which this single noise process does not separate from an artifact of the integrator. The numerical half is testable; the biological reading is not.

assessments.operationalization: For the models that show UCS-based memory, rescore the response after delays of 10 and 100 times the initial wait, with and without an intervening recall test. Most models keeping at least half their memories at the longest delay, and recall rarely erasing them, would confirm the claim; majority loss, or recall systematically destroying the trace, would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: time-lag UCS memory evaluator

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: pathway ODEs whose post-training trajectories are extended

obstacles: The initial waiting period is model-relative, so the 100-fold delay must be taken from the same definition as the code.
assessments.rationale: Persistence and recall are defined as delayed readouts of the same response variable, and a dedicated time-lag script is in the public repository along with the source models. Re-running that assay on the UCS-memory subset confirms or refutes both the long-delay retention claim and the claim about recall. The computation is heavy but specified.

assessments.operationalization: Train two associative memories in series, and separately two UCS-based memories in series and in parallel, on the biological models and the size-matched random models. Loss of both associative memories in every model, together with retention of paired UCS memories, would confirm the claim; retention of serial associative pairs, or failure of serial UCS pairs, would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: serial and parallel two-memory evaluation routines

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: biological ODE models paired with size-matched random circuits
