obstacles: Catastrophic forgetting is scored only for node triples that already passed the single-memory screen, so the denominator is selected.
assessments.rationale: Serial versus parallel training and the four pair types are specified, and the repository implements two-memory tests for biological and size-matched random models. Re-running those pairings decides whether associative pairs are uniformly lost while UCS pairs are not. The result is a property of this protocol, which is exactly the claim's scope.

assessments.operationalization: Label each of the 35 models by the source taxon class recorded in BioModels and test whether memory prevalence is homogeneous across bacteria, slime mould, yeast, plants, vertebrates and mammals. A clearly uneven distribution would refute uniformity inside this set; a flat distribution would support only that limited census.

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: organism annotations for the surveyed pathway models

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: per-model memory counts to stratify by taxon

obstacles: Class sizes in a 35-model curated list are too small for a uniformity test to be stable.
Uniformity among published models does not measure proto-cognitive capacity across living taxa.
assessments.rationale: Organism metadata and memory counts are both recoverable, so the distribution inside this list can be rechecked. The list is not a sample of life, and 'roughly uniformly' plus the suggestion about all strata of life outruns what 35 published models can show. The test covers a thin proxy for the stated scope.

assessments.operationalization: Apply six lengthening UCS stimulations and score a node pair as habituating when the response falls by at least half at each step. At least one such pair in each of the 27 testable models, with pair fractions between 1 and 50 percent, would confirm the claim; any testable model with zero pairs, or fractions outside that range, would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: pharmacoresistance and habituation screen, including saved result matrices

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: ODE models on which the six-pulse protocol is run

obstacles: Eight of the 35 models were dropped as untestable, so the 'every model' result is conditional on that filter.
Habituation here is a 50 percent ODE ratio, not a measured drug response.
assessments.rationale: The 50 percent criterion, the six increasing epochs and the 27-model denominator are explicit, and the repository contains the resistance screen plus result matrices. Re-running or reanalysing that screen can confirm or refute both the universal occurrence and the 1–50 percent band. The pharmacoresistance label is the authors' mapping, but the numerical claim is about the ODE assay.

assessments.operationalization: Compare the distribution of habituating pair fractions in the biological models with the 500 random circuits, using a 30 percent pair-fraction cutoff. A biological distribution shifted above that random ceiling would reproduce the contrast; overlap would remove the stated hint. Neither result identifies evolutionary pressure as the cause.

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: habituation scores for biological and random ODE networks

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: published pathway models treated as the evolved arm of the contrast

obstacles: The random circuits are not evolutionarily naive versions of the same pathways.
Curated published models are enriched for interesting dynamics independently of selection.
assessments.rationale: The biological-versus-random habituation contrast can be recomputed. The claim that pharmacoresistance is an adaptation produced by evolutionary pressure does not follow from that contrast, because model-building bias and a mismatched equation class are equally compatible with the same numbers. Only a weak proxy is testable now.

assessments.operationalization: After establishing habituation, stimulate each third node for up to three trials and count a model as breakable if any stimulus–response pair loses the 50 percent decline. Breaks in 17 of 27 models would confirm the count; a substantially different model count would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: third-node pharmacoresistance-breaking search and saved break matrices

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: pathway ODEs whose non-stimulus, non-response nodes are the candidate breakers

obstacles: A third-node clamp in an ODE is not yet a deliverable drug stimulus in cells.
assessments.rationale: The breaking rule, the three-trial cap and the 27-model base are specified, and the repository includes the breaking analysis. Re-running it decides whether about 63 percent of the habituating models contain at least one effective third node. That is the claim's actual scope; the therapeutic wording is carried by the same in silico count.

assessments.operationalization: Score a pair as sensitizing when the response rises at least 1.5-fold across six lengthening stimulations, and compare the fraction of biological models that have any such pair with the per-model pair rate in the random circuits. Twenty-seven of 35 biological models, against under 10 percent of random pairings, would reproduce the counts; a high random rate would refute uniqueness.

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: sensitization screen for biological and random models

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: biological pathway ODEs in the 35-model set

obstacles: The random null uses a different ODE family, so rarity there does not show the behaviour is unique to biology.
The paper itself allows that more complex random models might show sensitization.
assessments.rationale: The 1.5-fold rule and both arms of the comparison can be rerun from public code and BioModels. The biological count is a direct check. The inference that sensitization is unique to biology, or requires more complex random models, is not identified by this null, so the claim is only partly resolved by the rerun.

assessments.operationalization: On each sensitizing model, apply the third-node breaking protocol and record whether the 1.5-fold rise is abolished, and for what fraction of pairs. Breaks confined to 8 of 27 models and mostly under 5 percent of pairs, at a lower rate than habituation breaking, would confirm the claim; breaks in most models or in large pair fractions would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: sensitization-breaking trials comparable to the habituation-breaking trials

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: ODE models in which third-node interventions are simulated

obstacles: The comparison with habituation uses the same style of search, but the pair denominators differ across models.
assessments.rationale: Both breaking assays use an explicit ratio rule and a third-node search, and the code covers sensitization as well as pharmacoresistance. Re-running them yields the 8-of-27 count and the pair-fraction comparison directly. The remark about therapies needing other avenues is an interpretation of that same rate difference.

assessments.operationalization: Generate random ODEs matched on node count, edge count, in- and out-degree, betweenness, PageRank and hubness, then compare their memory rates with the biological models. Similar memory despite the match would refute insufficiency of those features; a large memory gap would support insufficiency only for this generator.

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: topology-matched random-network generator and memory scores

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: biological graphs that define the matching targets

obstacles: Matching those summaries does not match kinetics, signs of regulation or motifs.
Failure of one random generator does not show the features are useless for every design or evolutionary process.
assessments.rationale: The matching list and the memory comparison can be recomputed. A gap shows that this particular match is not sufficient inside this generator, which is weaker than the general design-and-evolution claim. Kinetics that were never matched remain a standing confound.

assessments.operationalization: Split BioModels ODE pathways into those with and without a strong oscillatory component, rerun the noise memory assay, and test whether the noise-associated memory gain is larger in the oscillatory group. A reliably larger gain would support the hypothesis; a null or reversed difference would count against it.

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: cell-cycle, circadian and other oscillatory pathway ODEs beyond the original highlights

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: noise assay whose memory gains can be stratified by oscillatory dynamics

obstacles: Only a handful of oscillatory models were singled out, and the paper already notes exceptions.
'Strong oscillatory component' and 'benefit more' need cutoffs the hypothesis does not fix.
assessments.rationale: Public circadian and cell-cycle models plus the noise script can test whether noise-linked memory gains cluster in oscillators. The hypothesis is hedged, the original contrast is tiny, and the authors already report oscillatory models that do not fit. A reanalysis can probe the association, not establish a general resonance rule.

assessments.operationalization: Randomly delete and add edges in biological and random models, rescore memory, and compare the drop. A significantly smaller drop for the biological models would confirm the robustness contrast; a similar or larger drop would refute it. The same curves do not test evolutionary pressure.

candidate_datasets.name: GRN_ODE
candidate_datasets.role: edge-perturbation robustness scripts for biological and random networks

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: biological pathway structures that are rewired in the assay

obstacles: Edge add and delete on an ODE needs a rule for new kinetic parameters, which can dominate the memory change.
Greater robustness is compatible with curation bias as well as with selection.
assessments.rationale: A robustness script is public, so the biological-versus-random degradation contrast can be rerun. The claim's causal clause, that the gap is perhaps due to evolutionary pressure to handle changing environments, is not identified by edge edits. The measurable half is the robustness difference alone.

assessments.operationalization: In living cells, record pulsatile signals from one cell and test whether a neighbour's pathway shows a persistent, specific change in a later response that meets the paper's memory criteria and that is absent without the pulses. That paired result would support in vivo behaviour-shaping; pulses without a lasting change in the neighbour would count against it.
obstacles: Public pulse-imaging studies do not pair an intercellular pulse train with a later memory assay on the target pathway.
The role in evolution and development is explicitly left unknown, so phenotype complexity alone does not decide it.
assessments.rationale: The in vivo claim needs timed stimuli between cells and a persistent change in the receiver pathway. Existing pathway models show in silico trainability, and pulsatile transcription is reported in the literature, but no public dataset contains both sides of this interaction. A decisive test would be a new, or newly deposited, paired measurement.

assessments.operationalization: Test whether identical or near-identical genotypes yield systematically different phenotypes under documented developmental conditions, using variant-to-trait catalogues and regeneration or polyphenism studies. Widespread genotype–phenotype non-isomorphism would support the negative half; a direct, one-to-one encoding across developmental contexts would refute it. Calling developmental physiology the control layer remains a further interpretation.

candidate_datasets.name: NHGRI-EBI GWAS Catalog
candidate_datasets.role: public variant–trait associations as a proxy for indirect genotype–phenotype maps

obstacles: GWAS misses developmental dynamics, so it cannot show that physiology is the layer selection evaluates.
Several evo-devo descriptions fit the same genotype–phenotype gaps.
assessments.rationale: Public genetic-association data can document that genotypes do not map cleanly onto phenotypes, which is the empirical core of the negative clause. They do not measure developmental physiology as a control layer between genomes and selection. The framework claim is only partly pinned to existing data, and rival wordings fit the same catalogues.

assessments.operationalization: Compile chromosome-count distributions for fissiparous planarians and fragment-level regeneration outcomes from deposited genomes, PlanMine records and published karyotype and amputation series. Variable ploidy together with near-complete restoration of anatomy would support the claim; a stable karyotype, or frequent regeneration failure, would refute the corresponding half.

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Datasets genomes
candidate_datasets.role: public planarian assemblies whose fragmentation and heterozygosity reflect the difficult genome

obstacles: Mixoploidy is mostly cytogenetic and is scattered across papers rather than stored as a single count dataset.
Regeneration success is size- and species-dependent, so 'every fragment' is stronger than typical published series.
assessments.rationale: Assemblies and PlanMine document a difficult Schmidtea genome, and many regeneration series report reliable restoration, but neither resource is a systematic census of chromosome number per cell or of every fragment. The two halves of the claim can be checked only by compiling biased published measurements. Coverage is a subset of fissiparous planarians, not the full stated scope.

assessments.operationalization: Compare the fitness cost of building a learning nervous system with the marginal cost of cellular sensing, sorting and motility in multicellular species, against the presence of those cellular behaviours in unicellular relatives. Competencies that are phylogenetically ancestral and costless to maintain would support the claim; a measurable extra cost, or independent origin inside metazoans, would count against 'by default'.
obstacles: No public dataset prices the marginal cost of cellular competencies against the cost of nervous-system learning.
Presence of similar behaviours in unicells does not show they were retained for free.
assessments.rationale: The contrast is empirical in principle: costs and phylogenetic origins could be measured. Comparative descriptions of unicellular behaviour exist, but they do not contain the cost accounting the claim requires, and the authors note elsewhere that real competency costs are unmeasured. Existing observations do not yet decide it.

assessments.operationalization: Rerun the public 1D embryogeny experiment at the published competency levels, including 400, and at the hardwired setting, and record generations until high phenotypic fitness. Competent populations reaching that fitness faster and more consistently, on the order of under 6 generations versus over 200, would confirm the claim; overlapping times would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: CellularCompetency
candidate_datasets.role: Python simulation and hyperparameters for competent versus hardwired 1D embryos

obstacles: Exact generation counts depend on the published mutation rate, selection stringency and fitness definition.
assessments.rationale: Fitness is an explicit inversion count, competency is a bounded bubble-sort, and the competent-versus-hardwired experiment is a public script with hyperparameters. A small team can rerun it in days to weeks and compare time-to-fitness. The claim is about this model, and the code covers that scope.

assessments.operationalization: From the same runs, plot genotypic fitness of the best competent individuals against hardwired controls across generations, and compare variance at higher competency. A brief rise then a plateau below the hardwired trajectory, with wider variance at higher competency, would confirm the claim; genotypic fitness tracking phenotypic fitness would refute reduced selective pressure.

candidate_datasets.name: CellularCompetency
candidate_datasets.role: records genotypic and phenotypic fitness for competent and hardwired populations

obstacles: Plateau height depends on how many bubble-sort steps the competency parameter allows.
assessments.rationale: The model stores genotypic order separately from post-sorting phenotypic order, and the public experiment already runs the competency sweep. Reanalysis of those runs confirms or refutes the plateau and the variance pattern. No extra biological dataset is required because the claim is about this simulation.

assessments.operationalization: Rerun mixed populations of 200 embryos at the stated initial competent fractions, including 2.5, 10, 20 and 30 percent, across competency levels, and record whether competent genomes exceed half the population within two or three generations. Dominance thresholds near 75, 40 and 10, and failure at 2.5 percent even at competency 95, would confirm the claim; dominance at 2.5 percent or failure at the higher shares would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: CellularCompetency
candidate_datasets.role: mixed-population and minority-competent evolutionary runs

obstacles: The default hyperparameter file does not list every fraction in the claim, so some grid points must be set from the paper.
assessments.rationale: Takeover is a head-count in a fully specified genetic algorithm, and the mixed-population script is public. A few fraction-by-competency cells may need to be set from the paper rather than the default JSON, which is still reimplementation of a stated model. The numerical thresholds can be confirmed or refuted by those runs.

assessments.operationalization: Evolve the competency allele from a low initial range over 1000 generations and record the best individual's competency. A rapid rise that plateaus near 470, above the competency needed for maximum fitness, would confirm the trajectory; a low plateau or continued directional climb would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: CellularCompetency
candidate_datasets.role: evolvable-competency experiment that logs the competency allele

obstacles: Attributing the excess over the fitness-maximizing value to drift requires showing a fitness plateau, not just a high mean.
Stochastic runs will not reproduce the exact path up to 485.
assessments.rationale: The evolvable-competency script is public and the decision variable is the competency allele itself. Re-running it tests the rapid rise and high plateau. Exact meander values will differ across seeds, but the claimed plateau near 470 versus the fitness threshold is a stable summary a small team can estimate.

assessments.operationalization: In the evolvable-competency runs, compute the correlation of genotypic and phenotypic fitness each generation. A fall to about zero by generation 20, while phenotypic fitness stays high, would confirm the claim; a correlation that remains strongly positive would refute decoupling.

candidate_datasets.name: CellularCompetency
candidate_datasets.role: paired genotypic and phenotypic fitness time series under evolvable competency

obstacles: The generation at which correlation hits zero is seed-sensitive and should be summarized over repeats.
assessments.rationale: Both fitnesses are defined in the model and emitted by the evolvable-competency experiment. A correlation trajectory is a standard calculation on those outputs. If the correlation stays high, the claim that evolving competency blocks selection on structural genes in this model is refuted.

assessments.operationalization: Subtract a penalty proportional to competency, over factors from 1e-7 to 0.5, from fitness in the public evolvable-competency loop, and track structural-gene fitness and the competency allele. Continued structural improvement, declining competency and later genetic assimilation would confirm the simulated Baldwin effect; competency staying high, or structural fitness stalling, would refute it at that cost.

candidate_datasets.name: CellularCompetency
candidate_datasets.role: base evolutionary loop to which the published competency penalty can be added

obstacles: The public scripts and hyperparameter file do not expose the fitness-penalty experiment as a turnkey run.
Real organismal costs are unmeasured, so the simulation does not say which penalty factor is biological.
assessments.rationale: The penalty rule and the factor range are stated, and the underlying simulator is public, so the Baldwin runs can be reimplemented as an extension rather than a new kind of model. They are not a packaged experiment in the repository, and some controls sit in the supplement. The in silico claim is testable with that extra assembly; it does not measure real competency costs.

assessments.operationalization: Compare planarian genome disorder and anatomical fidelity with other animals, and ask whether lineages with messier genomes and more regenerative competency show the model's signature of weakened selection on structural genes. The messy-genome plus reliable-anatomy pattern can be checked; the historical claim that competency ran away because selection could not see structural genes cannot.

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Datasets genomes
candidate_datasets.role: comparative assemblies for genome contiguity versus regenerative taxa

obstacles: Asexuality, abundant stem cells and bioelectric control explain the same pattern without a competency ratchet.
No dataset records historical selective pressure on planarian structural genes.
assessments.rationale: Public genomes and regeneration records can reassess the paradoxical pattern the authors want explained. They cannot show that selection shifted onto generic competency because structural defects were hidden. Several non-ratchet histories fit the same present-day facts, so only a proxy pattern is testable.

assessments.operationalization: Search PlanMine phenotype records and the planarian literature for stable, heritable, morphologically abnormal strains, and separate them from RNAi knockdowns and from the bioelectrically induced two-headed line. A heritable morphological mutant line would refute the universal negative; finding only the two-headed bioelectric line would support it under a strict definition of genetic strain.

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: literature index for reports of planarian morphological mutant lines and the two-headed strain

obstacles: RNAi morphological phenotypes are easily counted as genetic strains.
The negative claim is definition- and date-sensitive, and sexual-strain genetics are sparsely reported.
assessments.rationale: Whether abnormal genetic strains have been reported is a census of public records, and PlanMine plus the literature are the right places to look. The census does not cleanly separate stable mutants, clonal anomalies and transient knockdowns, and it cannot show that the model predicted the two-headed line rather than accommodating it. The empirical half is only partly decidable.

assessments.operationalization: In the evolvable-competency runs, attribute each positional change to either the competency allele or one of the fifty structural genes and compare change frequencies. A significantly higher competency-gene rate would reproduce the count; similar rates would refute it. The comparison still has to rule out an artifact of the allele's numeric range.

candidate_datasets.name: CellularCompetency
candidate_datasets.role: frequency comparison of competency-gene versus structural-gene changes

obstacles: A competency allele ranging toward 500 can register more changes than a positional gene for mechanical reasons.
Mutation rate and representation are not matched per locus in a way that isolates evolutionary effort.
assessments.rationale: The public experiment can plot how often the competency gene changes relative to structural genes, so the reported inequality is re-computable. That inequality does not cleanly mean evolution works on competency more, because one wide-ranged competency locus is not comparable to fifty structural loci without a normalization the claim does not apply. The raw count is testable; the effort interpretation is confounded.

assessments.operationalization: In the 1D model, test whether hiding genotypic defects from selection produces a positive feedback in which competency keeps rising while structural-gene improvement stalls. That loop can be confirmed or refuted in the simulation. No existing dataset measures the same ratchet across real developmental systems or other problem spaces.

candidate_datasets.name: CellularCompetency
candidate_datasets.role: 1D embryogeny model in which the proposed feedback can be re-simulated

obstacles: The model equates competency with bubble-sort steps on a monotonic axis, which is a narrow proxy for intelligence.
A positive feedback in this GA does not show a ratchet in evolving organisms.
assessments.rationale: The suggested ratchet is readable as a dynamical pattern in a public, fully specified toy evolution, so that pattern can be rerun. The claim then generalizes to an intelligence ratchet in developmental evolution and other spaces. Nothing public measures problem-solving competency and structural-gene selection jointly across real lineages, so only the model proxy is testable.

assessments.operationalization: No public observation separates 'problem-solving competency drove evolution before brains' from the statement that developmental mechanisms affected fitness before nervous systems existed. Fossils and phylogenies show early morphological complexity either way.
obstacles: Pre-neural morphological complexity is compatible with competency as a driver and with competency as a label for ordinary development.
No dataset records problem-solving competency as a causal variable in deep time.
assessments.rationale: The authors equate intelligence with problem-solving competency and assert it was an evolutionary driver before brains. A non-cognitive description of the same early bodies and developmental mechanisms fits every available fossil and phylogenetic pattern. The claim does not add a measurement that would decide between those descriptions.

assessments.operationalization: Rerun ES-HyperNEAT on the public 2D neural cellular automaton, with cell reward tied only to energy and stripe match, and measure whether the tissue reaches a three-band French-flag pattern. Reliable high pattern accuracy would support the scaling result in this model; consistent failure to pattern would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: scalefreecognition
candidate_datasets.role: Python Mesa and MultiNEAT implementation of the French-flag tissue model

obstacles: The repository sets a debug generation count and analysis expects a parameter file that is not in the tree.
Evolutionary runs are stochastic, so exact published accuracies need either saved genomes or many full replications.
assessments.rationale: Pattern accuracy is a direct fitness readout, and the model code is public, so the French-flag result can be attempted without new biological data. The snapshot is not a complete reproduction package, and ES-HyperNEAT runs are slow and stochastic. A rerun can test whether such collectives arise, not recover every reported percentage from the original seeds.

assessments.operationalization: Initialize the same evolved tissues from a homogeneous cell state and from random cell states and compare final French-flag accuracy. A reliable drop under random initialization would support the simulation half; equal accuracy would refute it. Matching that preference to real embryos is a separate, qualitative analogy.

candidate_datasets.name: scalefreecognition
candidate_datasets.role: tissue model whose initial cell states can be set homogeneous or random

obstacles: The comparison is described for the evolved system, and champion genomes are not deposited.
'Less well' is not given a numeric margin, and the embryo analogy is not a measurement in the model.
assessments.rationale: The initial-condition contrast is well defined inside the simulator and could be run if a competent genome is in hand. The public code does not include the saved tissues, and the claim also treats the result as what real development does. The simulation contrast is a partial test; the embryological generalization is not resolved by it.

assessments.operationalization: Select only on French-flag accuracy over the first 100 steps, then at step 110 flip two columns of the red stripe to white, and separately flip the whole stripe, and score restoration. Recovery from the small edit and failure on the whole stripe would confirm the claim; failure on small edits, or recovery from the whole-stripe edit, would refute the stated boundary.

candidate_datasets.name: scalefreecognition
candidate_datasets.role: neural cellular automaton in which post-development perturbations can be applied

obstacles: Without deposited genomes, re-evolution may not yield a tissue with the same repair range.
Fitness must be checked to stop at 100 steps so repair is not accidentally rewarded.
assessments.rationale: The perturbation sizes, the timing and the selection window are specified, and the model code exposes cell states. Reproducing the repair result still depends on recovering or re-evolving the tissues, which the repository does not archive. The qualitative repair claim is testable by re-evolution; the exact published boundary is only partly recoverable.

assessments.operationalization: Run an unperturbed evolved tissue past pattern stabilization and test whether each burst of cell-state change is immediately preceded by a spike in the model's stress variable. Spikes leading every remodelling onset would support the temporal claim; remodelling without a prior spike, or spikes that do not lead activity, would refute it. Precedence still would not prove that stress drives the change.

candidate_datasets.name: scalefreecognition
candidate_datasets.role: simulation logs of stress and cell state over long unperturbed runs

obstacles: The result is reported for a representative individual, not as a pre-registered rate across tissues.
A spike before movement is compatible with a common cause inside the network.
assessments.rationale: Stress and morphogenetic activity are both variables in the public model, so lead-lag can be recomputed on long runs. The published observation is one tissue's trace, and the causal wording goes beyond precedence. Re-simulation can check whether spikes lead remodelling in this system, not that stress is the driver in general.

assessments.operationalization: Evolve tissues with fitness evaluated only over 100 steps, then continue selected individuals to 1000 steps and measure pattern accuracy. Maintenance at or above developmental accuracy would support allostasis without direct selection; collapse after step 100 would refute it in this model.

candidate_datasets.name: scalefreecognition
candidate_datasets.role: developmental simulator whose step limit can be extended past the fitness window

obstacles: Intrinsic dynamics can maintain a pattern for trivial dynamical reasons that are not regenerative capacity.
Saved adult trajectories are not in the repository, and 1000-step reruns are costly.
assessments.rationale: The selection window and the 1000-step probe are explicit, and the code's developmental horizon is the 100-step fitness period. Extending a run tests maintenance. Because champion genomes are not deposited and long ES-HyperNEAT searches are specialist work, the claim is recoverable only by a partial, stochastic re-evolution rather than a direct replay.

assessments.operationalization: On a tissue that uses stress instructively, clamp stress to zero for the whole run and compare pattern accuracy and red-stripe survival with the unclamped run. Accuracy near 82.8 percent versus 95.1 percent at step 90, plus loss of the red stripe, would reproduce the result; unchanged accuracy would refute dependence in that tissue.

candidate_datasets.name: scalefreecognition
candidate_datasets.role: stress variable that can be clamped as the simulated anxiolytic

obstacles: The percentages belong to one evolved tissue that is not archived in the repository.
Re-evolved tissues often solve the flag without using stress, so a random rerun may not be the stress-using case.
assessments.rationale: Zeroing stress and reading pattern accuracy is a well-specified intervention in the model. The claim is about one stress-using individual and two precise percentages, and those genomes are not public. A new evolution can look for the phenomenon, but it will not reliably replay this tissue, so the stated result is only partly resolvable.

assessments.operationalization: Impose a range of constant stress levels on an already patterned tissue and record the immediate and delayed change in cell state. Effects confined to particular concentrations, including no immediate change at a very high level followed by a later change, would support a level-specific code; graded immediate effects at all levels would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: scalefreecognition
candidate_datasets.role: evolved tissue model in which external stress levels can be imposed

obstacles: 'Specific concentrations' is illustrated rather than given as a full dose-response criterion.
The encoding is a property of particular evolved networks, which are not deposited.
assessments.rationale: Stress level and cell state are measurable in the simulator, so a dose sweep is possible once a tissue exists. The claim reports one qualitative pattern, delayed change after very high stress, and reads it as an evolved code. Without the original networks, re-evolution tests whether some codes are level-specific, not this reported encoding.

assessments.operationalization: Evolve or reload ten high-fitness tissues, disable stress, and count how many die, then change the target morphology mid-run and compare the stress-using tissue with the others. One death in ten, plus a higher score for the stress-using tissue under the target change with p near 0.03, would reproduce the claim; many deaths, or no accuracy gap, would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: scalefreecognition
candidate_datasets.role: evolutionary runs that can be repeated with stress clamped and with a mid-run target change

obstacles: The p-value contrasts one stress-using tissue with nine others and will not recur from new seeds.
Ten full ES-HyperNEAT evolutions are a large compute job, and genomes were not released.
assessments.rationale: Death without stress and accuracy after a target change are defined readouts, and the code can express both interventions. The claim's numbers are properties of ten particular evolutionary outcomes that are not in the repository. A new sample can estimate the rates, but it cannot confirm or refute p = 0.0312 for that sample, and the compute is beyond a quick standard analysis.

assessments.operationalization: On the original unperturbed runs, compute transfer entropy from each cell's stress to its own next state and to its neighbours' states. A substantially larger neighbour term would support paracrine dominance; a larger self term would support autocrine dominance and refute the claim.

candidate_datasets.name: scalefreecognition
candidate_datasets.role: tissue trajectories and analysis code for active information and transfer entropy

obstacles: Transfer entropy depends on binning, history length and which evolved tissue is logged.
The analysis script expects a general parameter file that is not in the repository, and the trajectories are not archived.
assessments.rationale: Paracrine versus autocrine use is operationalized as a comparison of two transfer entropies, which is a standard calculation on simulation logs. Those logs and a complete analysis configuration are not in the public snapshot, so the comparison requires regenerating tissues first. The test is well posed and only partly feasible with what was released.

assessments.operationalization: On logged cell-state time series from the evolved French-flag network, compute pairwise local transfer entropy between red and white stripe cells with history k = 4, as defined in the paper. A red-to-white peak before about step 60 followed by a larger white-to-red peak confirms the reported reversal; no reversal, or a reversal that disappears under alternate binning, refutes it.

candidate_datasets.name: Scale-free cognition neural cellular automaton
candidate_datasets.role: public Python implementation of the evolved French-flag tissue; the committed tree does not include winner_net.txt or the logged trajectories

candidate_datasets.name: Java Information Dynamics Toolkit
candidate_datasets.role: standard library for the local transfer entropy the paper uses to compare stripes

obstacles: The published winner network and cell-state time series are not in the repository, and the committed run.py uses a two-generation demonstration setting.
Transfer entropy is computed on one representative individual; stripe-to-stripe sums are confounded by which cells are actually changing state.
Directed information flow is not a graft assay, so it does not show that a stripe instructively induces pattern in the other.
assessments.rationale: The information-theoretic contrast is specified tightly enough, and the model code is public, that recomputing stripe-to-stripe transfer entropy is analysis rather than a new experiment. What is missing is the evolved network and the traces behind the published peaks, so a re-evolution tests whether the reversal is a typical output, not whether the reported run had it. The organizer reading remains a gloss on that asymmetry.

assessments.operationalization: Average local transfer entropy from each cell's energy to its state, and the reverse, across the tissue time series. An energy-to-state peak near step 55 that precedes overlap of the two directions would confirm the reported order; a first peak in the opposite direction, or simultaneous rise, would refute the order.

candidate_datasets.name: Scale-free cognition neural cellular automaton
candidate_datasets.role: public model in which energy and cell state are explicit variables; saved analysis trajectories are not deposited

candidate_datasets.name: Java Information Dynamics Toolkit
candidate_datasets.role: implementation of local transfer entropy between energy and cell state

obstacles: Saved energy and state traces for the reported run are not in the code repository.
A lead of energy-to-state transfer entropy is compatible with a common driver and does not establish top-down control of survival energy.
assessments.rationale: The peak-order comparison can be rerun once energy and state are logged from the public model, using the paper's definition of local transfer entropy. The deposited code does not include those logs or the winner network, and the further statement that the anatomical loop controls single-cell energy is not identified by peak order alone. A re-evolved tissue can test the qualitative order, not the published figure.

assessments.operationalization: Plot mean local active information storage of cell state against stress in the same runs, with stress discretized in chunks of 10. Stress rising while active information storage of the white and red stripes falls, then the reverse as stress falls, would confirm the reported concurrence; stress spikes with flat or rising storage would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Scale-free cognition neural cellular automaton
candidate_datasets.role: public simulation with explicit stress and cell-state variables; the information-storage analysis itself is not implemented in the repository

candidate_datasets.name: Java Information Dynamics Toolkit
candidate_datasets.role: library for local active information storage on the cell-state series

obstacles: The blue stripe has zero active information storage because those cells never change state, so the tissue average is structurally biased.
The reported concurrence is from a representative run, and the winner network is not deposited.
assessments.rationale: Stress and active information storage are defined quantitatively, so their timing can be recomputed from logged runs of the public model. The repository does not contain the analyzed trajectories, and the evolutionary claim that stress was recruited as a channel for failed prediction is an interpretation of a correlation. Re-evolution would speak to whether the correlation is typical.

assessments.operationalization: Follow individual regenerating or developing animals after an apparently stable phenotype and record whether anatomy changes again without a new intervention, using the planarian cutoff of any morphology change after four weeks. Repeated independent cohorts in which a non-trivial fraction remodel after long stability would support the prediction; large cohorts followed well past that window with no late change would count against it.
obstacles: The wording is that something similar may occur, so failure to see late remodelling does not refute it.
No public animal-level longitudinal morphology table covers the weeks after apparent regenerative completion.
Late change can be produced by starvation, infection, or residual drug rather than an intrinsic return to an anatomical trajectory.
assessments.rationale: The planarian version of the prediction is measurable, but the only quantitative series is this paper's own aggregate, and the supplementary file is a document of figures rather than a reusable cohort table. Independent long-term imaging after a scored stable phenotype is not in a public dataset. Re-reading the paper's figure is not a test of the prediction.

assessments.operationalization: Score each Dugesia japonica pre-tail fragment treated with 18 μM U0126 for three days, kept individually until death, for any morphology change after four weeks, and among those for return to one head. A recount near 22% of about 181 animals, mostly between four and ten weeks, with about 61% of the changers restoring one head, would confirm the report; a recount far from those fractions, or an independent cohort at the same dose with almost no late change, would refute it.
obstacles: Animal-level weekly scores are not deposited; the public record is the summary and figure 10.
The scoring rubric counts fission and dorsal or lateral outgrowths as repatterning, and fission creates a new wound.
Headless animals cannot feed, so late change is confounded with prolonged starvation.
assessments.rationale: The dose, fragment type, follow-up, and phenotype classes are explicit, so a recount would decide the percentages. Those worm-by-worm scores are not in a public table, and the figshare supplement is a supplementary document rather than the scoring sheet. Without that sheet or an independent cohort, the published summary cannot be checked.

assessments.operationalization: Compare the latency from completed regeneration to spontaneous anatomical change in ERK-inhibited headless Dugesia with the published time to a stable regenerate in untreated fragments of the same species. Latencies of many weeks, well beyond the usual one-to-two-week regenerative window, would support a slower tissue process; latencies inside the ordinary window, or late changes explained by drug persistence or starvation, would count against it.
obstacles: The latency distribution is not available as a public individual-level table.
A slow residual effect of U0126, or injury from late fission, mimics a newly discovered slow tissue process.
assessments.rationale: A timescale comparison is well posed only if the late-change events and a baseline regenerative schedule can be aligned animal by animal. The late events are not deposited beyond the paper's summary, so the inference to an unknown slow process cannot be separated from drug, wound, or starvation alternatives with existing public records.

assessments.operationalization: In runs of the evolved tissue, measure distance to the French-flag target over time and read the fitness function in the code. A transient increase in distance while misplaced cells are removed, followed by return, in a model whose fitness does not reward that excursion or long-term maintenance, would support the simulation result; monotonic approach, or a fitness term that penalizes intermediate error, would refute the unselected-excursion reading.

candidate_datasets.name: Scale-free cognition neural cellular automaton
candidate_datasets.role: public evolutionary model whose fitness evaluation and tissue dynamics can be inspected; paper hyperparameters and winner networks are not committed

obstacles: Whether intermediate error is invisible to selection depends on whether fitness is an endpoint score or a time integral, which has to be read out of the model class rather than a deposited results table.
The committed script is a short demonstration configuration, so it is not a replay of the published 1000-step runs.
assessments.rationale: The excursion away from the target and the contents of the fitness function can be checked by running and reading the public model, which is analysis. The repository does not contain the published long runs, and the step from this fitness function to unselected capabilities of multi-scale homeostatic systems generally is outside what one simulation decides. Endpoint versus cumulative fitness is a real ambiguity in the test.

assessments.operationalization: Classify each late planarian morphology change by whether a new wound, fission, or bite occurred in the preceding interval. Events with no wound would support initiation without a missing-tissue response; restriction of late heads to post-fission wounds would count against it.
obstacles: The paper's own repatterning classes include fission, which opens a wound, and those classes are not deposited animal by animal.
A possibility claim that a missing-tissue response may be unnecessary is weakly refutable.
assessments.rationale: Whether a new injury preceded each late regenerative event is decidable from longitudinal notes, and those notes are not public. The aggregate result mixes fission with other morphology changes, so the existing summary does not separate regeneration-without-injury from regeneration-after-a-late-wound. A general claim about the missing-tissue response needs cohorts beyond this experiment.

assessments.operationalization: Compare published bacterial biofilm stress oscillations, vertebrate segmentation-clock time series, and stress-linked stripe formation in the French-flag model for a shared motif in which a metabolic or stress oscillation sets spatial boundaries. A common motif under a pre-specified distance on those series would support a shared dynamical pattern; qualitatively different mechanisms would count against it.

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: public kinetic models of segmentation clocks and other spatial oscillators, for a dynamical comparison rather than a homology test

candidate_datasets.name: Gene Expression Omnibus
candidate_datasets.role: time-resolved expression series during somitogenesis that can be compared with oscillator models

candidate_datasets.name: Scale-free cognition neural cellular automaton
candidate_datasets.role: the in silico stress-and-stripe system named in the comparison

obstacles: Shared oscillation-plus-pattern is compatible with analogy and does not show a conserved mechanism from bacteria to metazoans.
No single public dataset pairs biofilm nitrogen stress, vertebrate segmentation, and the neural cellular automaton under one schema.
assessments.rationale: Pieces of the comparison are public: segmentation-clock models and expression series, and the tissue simulation. They can test a restricted dynamical resemblance. They do not contain a cross-kingdom homology or a matched stress-to-pattern experiment, so the conservation reading stays underdetermined.

assessments.operationalization: A non-cognitive description, in which the same ion channels, stresses, and gene-regulatory loops implement physiological homeostasis at cell and tissue scale, predicts the same developmental and regenerative observations. No public measurement separates retained ancestral cognition scaled to anatomical goals from that physiological description, so there is no confirming or refuting outcome.
obstacles: Cognitive repertoire and anatomical goals have several contested operationalizations.
Comparative presence of ancient cell-biological machinery does not decide whether that machinery is cognition.
assessments.rationale: The historical and cognitive wording does not add an observation beyond multicellular use of conserved cellular control loops. Any dataset of channel genes, regeneration, or learning in unicells can be described without a retained cognitive repertoire. The claim is therefore not separated from its non-cognitive rival by existing data.

assessments.operationalization: Shared molecules and similar feedback structure in morphogenesis and behaviour are expected if neural control was exapted from older physiological signalling, with no scaling of goals. No measurement distinguishes that exaptation from a pivot of collective intelligence along one continuum, so the outcome of a comparative survey would not confirm or refute the proposal.
obstacles: Goal and collective intelligence are not tied to one measurement that rivals must fail.
A continuum claim is compatible with both deep homology of signalling parts and a cognitive redescription of the same parts.
assessments.rationale: Phylogenies of ion channels and transmitters can show reuse of physiological machinery in nervous systems. They cannot show that evolution pivoted collective intelligence by enlarging homeostatic setpoints, because a non-cognitive exaptation account fits the same genes and the same behaviours. The proposal has no discriminating observation.

assessments.operationalization: For published developmental models with an explicit genotype-to-anatomy map, attempt to recover parameter or genotype changes that produce a specified large-scale anatomical change, and compare success with and without a known route for somatic information to reach the germline. Systematic failure of inversion in well-specified models would support computational irreversibility as a barrier; reliable inversion, or empirical cases where a known edit produces a chosen organ-scale trait, would count against unsolvability as the limit on Lamarckian inheritance.

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: public dynamical models of development whose invertibility can be probed as a restricted proxy

candidate_datasets.name: Scale-free cognition neural cellular automaton
candidate_datasets.role: a fully specified generative map from evolved network to French-flag anatomy

obstacles: Unsolvability in general depends on the model class and is not read out of metazoan datasets.
Existing models cover a negligible fraction of real genotype-to-anatomy maps.
assessments.rationale: Inversion difficulty can be measured on public developmental models, which is analysis of a proxy. Those models do not establish that real morphogenesis is unsolvable or that this, rather than transmission to the germline, is what limits Lamarckian inheritance across metazoans. The claim's full scope is not in any dataset.

assessments.operationalization: In the public artificial-embryogeny model, compare the rate of fitness gain and the fraction of accepted changes in competency rules versus structural genes. Faster search and a shift toward competency edits would support a proxy in which evolution spends its effort on behaviour-shaping rules; equal or greater progress through structural edits would count against that proxy.

candidate_datasets.name: Cellular competency evolution model
candidate_datasets.role: public simulations and saved runs contrasting hardwired and competent development, the nearest explicit search process

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Datasets genomes
candidate_datasets.role: comparative gene repertoires for a weak proxy based on signalling versus structural genes

obstacles: The simulation searches a toy axial map, not the space of metazoan cell-behaviour rules.
Elevated evolution of signalling genes is compatible with ordinary selection on phenotypes and does not identify the search space.
assessments.rationale: The cited competency model is public, includes saved runs, and can show whether selection shifts onto competency parameters. That is a proxy for one sentence of a much broader claim about what evolution searches in metazoans. Sequence collections do not discriminate behaviour-shaping signals from the rest of the genome as the object of search.

assessments.operationalization: Compare public evolutionary runs that use a compressed generative encoding with otherwise matched direct encodings, and score robustness and success on environments not seen during selection. Higher novel-environment success for the generative encoding would support the architectural prediction; no difference, or a difference explained by parameter count alone, would count against it.

candidate_datasets.name: Cellular competency evolution model
candidate_datasets.role: public indirect developmental layer between genotype and the phenotype that selection sees

candidate_datasets.name: Scale-free cognition neural cellular automaton
candidate_datasets.role: public ES-HyperNEAT system in which a CPPN is a compressed generator of the cell network

obstacles: The autoencoder analogy is not a unique encoding, so several implementations can be called confirmatory.
Robustness in a toy embryogeny does not show that real evolution is pushed to general-purpose problem solvers.
assessments.rationale: Indirect encodings in the two public models can be scored for performance off the training conditions, which tests a narrow version of the architectural claim. Neither model is a variational autoencoder of a metazoan genome, and success in those runs would not show that evolution is freed from over-training or that plasticity in organisms is produced by that compression.

assessments.operationalization: Relate measured gap-junction coupling, or a specific blockade, to the spatial scale of a patterning outcome and to whether a transient stimulus still alters a later regenerative choice. Pattern scale shrinking under blockade, and memory of a stimulus surviving only when coupling is intact, would support the scaling claim; pattern scale and stimulus memory unchanged by coupling would count against it.
obstacles: Gap-junction blockers have off-target effects, and dye coupling is not memory or predictive capacity.
No public dataset pairs coupling strength with a later anatomical setpoint across tissues.
assessments.rationale: Blockade and dye-coupling experiments already published can speak to whether electrical coupling changes the scale of pattern, but they are scattered in papers rather than a downloadable table of memory radius against coupling. Xenbase covers gene annotations, not that functional pairing. Enlarged goal states are not distinguished from a change in physiological correlation length.

assessments.operationalization: Compare motility and collective behaviour of Xenopus embryonic epidermal cells dissociated from the embryo with intact embryonic epidermis. Self-motile aggregates formed from those cells, and absent while the cells remain in place, would support the explant result; failure to form motile constructs under the published dissociation protocol would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Reconfigurable organisms design code
candidate_datasets.role: public evolutionary design code for the Xenobot shapes; it does not hold the wet-lab motility recordings

obstacles: Ciliary motility used for mucus clearance in vivo can look like a novel behaviour once cells are free in culture.
Trial-level videos and counts sit in the original papers' supplements, not in an independent data repository.
assessments.rationale: The explant contrast is concrete and the design pipeline's code is public, but the biological outcome is documented as published experimental reports from the same research program rather than a reusable tracking dataset. Those reports can be checked for whether motile aggregates were produced. They do not isolate the neighbour signals supposed to suppress the behaviour, so the suppression clause stays partly untested.

assessments.operationalization: Date ion-channel and pump families on public bacterial and metazoan genomes and align that distribution with published biofilm electrical signalling. Channels and propagating ionic signals already present in biofilms would support early availability of the hardware; restriction of such signals to nervous systems would count against the timing.

candidate_datasets.name: UniProt
candidate_datasets.role: annotated ion-channel and pump sequences across bacteria and animals

candidate_datasets.name: NCBI Datasets genomes
candidate_datasets.role: public genomes for placing those families relative to biofilms and nervous systems

obstacles: Presence of a channel gene is not evidence that it was used to integrate information across a biofilm.
The purpose clause, that this is why brains use the same modality, is not a separate observable.
assessments.rationale: Public protein and genome collections can test whether the relevant electrical hardware is ancient and present in bacteria, which is the dating half of the statement. Published biofilm physiology is separate and not a single deposited time series here. Neither resource records an evolutionary discovery of information processing, as opposed to cells that happen to be electrically coupled.

assessments.operationalization: In Xenopus tadpoles, compare eye formation after misexpression of the specified ion channels that reproduce a facial voltage pattern in gut or tail, against the same sites after Pax6 delivery alone. Ectopic eyes at those sites after the voltage manipulation, and not after Pax6 there, would support the report; no ectopic eyes, or eyes induced equally by Pax6 outside the anterior neurectoderm, would refute it.
obstacles: The induction frequencies and voltage images are in the original papers' figures, not a public animal-level file.
Injected cells can recruit neighbours, so the competent tissue is not cleanly the injected territory alone.
assessments.rationale: Eye presence, injection site, and the Pax6 contrast are standard experimental variables, and the published Xenopus literature, indexed for this species in Xenbase, reports them. There is no open matrix of voltage pattern against organ outcome that an outside group can reprocess, and independent replication series are not a separate dataset. The test is therefore a reassessment of published measurements for this species, not a full reanalysis.

assessments.operationalization: Score visual learning in Xenopus tadpoles with native eyes prevented and one ectopic eye on the tail, and record whether that eye's axons enter the spinal cord or peripheral tissue rather than the brain. Learning above the no-eye and extraocular-photoreception controls would support seeing through the ectopic eye; chance performance, or learning that survives removal of the ectopic eye, would refute it.
obstacles: Extraocular light sensitivity can imitate vision unless the ectopic eye is covered or removed as a control.
The behavioural trials are published as summary performance, not as a public trial table.
assessments.rationale: The learning assay and the anatomical connection are concrete, and the 2013 experimental report gives published performance for this exact preparation. Those measurements can be reassessed against the stated controls, but they cannot be recomputed from raw choices, and Xenbase does not hold the trial file. The result is checkable as a published experiment, not as an open behavioural dataset.

assessments.operationalization: In polyploid newt kidney tubules, count cells per cross-section, cell size, and whether a single cell closes the lumen, compared with diploid tubules that use about eight to ten cells. A shift from a multicellular tube to one wrapped cell at higher ploidy would support the anatomical report; persistent multicellular tubes despite giant cells would refute it.
obstacles: The observations are mid-twentieth-century histological accounts, not a digital image archive.
Downward causation and the choice of cytoskeletal bending over cell-cell communication are interpretations of the same sections.
assessments.rationale: Cell number and lumen closure are measurable, and the classical newt literature reports them for this organ. There is no public image set from which the counts can be redone, so coverage is the published descriptions of one system. The goal-directed and downward-causation reading is not separated by those sections from a passive geometric consequence of enlarged cells.

assessments.operationalization: On any public model that contains ion-channel genotype, a bioelectric pattern, and an anatomical output, compare inversion error for the direct genotype-to-anatomy map with the two-step path through the bioelectric pattern. Lower error on both steps than on the direct map would support the decomposition; equal or worse error would refute it for that model.

candidate_datasets.name: BioModels
candidate_datasets.role: public dynamical models that can be searched for maps linking physiology to pattern; few encode genotype, voltage, and anatomy together

obstacles: Almost no deposited model contains all three layers with an invertible map.
Easier inversion in a model is not evidence about the historical control problem faced by evolution.
assessments.rationale: The two-step inversion comparison is a definite numerical test on a model that has both layers. Public model repositories rarely encode genotype, voltage, and anatomy together, so only a proxy analysis is available. The claim about real bioelectric control and about engineers is not settled by that proxy.

assessments.operationalization: Align yeast plasma-membrane proton-pump sequences and structures with Xenopus V-ATPase subunits, and compare tadpole tail regeneration when the yeast pump is expressed in place of V-ATPase function. Absence of significant sequence and structural homology, together with rescue of regeneration and of the regenerative voltage, would support interchangeability of the voltage state; homology, or rescue without restoration of voltage, would count against voltage as the instructive variable.

candidate_datasets.name: UniProt
candidate_datasets.role: sequences of the yeast proton pump and vertebrate V-ATPase subunits for a homology test

candidate_datasets.name: RCSB Protein Data Bank
candidate_datasets.role: structures for the same proteins, to test the no-structural-homology clause

obstacles: The tail-regeneration rescue counts are in the original experimental paper, not in UniProt or the PDB.
A yeast pump could restore regeneration by changing pH independently of the voltage pattern the claim treats as the signal.
assessments.rationale: The homology half can be settled directly from public sequences and structures. The functional phenocopy is a specific Xenopus regeneration result published as experimental measurements, without a deposited animal-level regeneration file in these databases. Voltage as the coarse-grained instructive variable is supported only if the rescue is tied to the bioelectric state rather than to a side effect of proton pumping.

assessments.operationalization: Treat memory as a regenerative head number that stays altered after a brief physiological treatment is washed out, in animals whose genotype is the wild-type stock, and that can be reset by a later physiological treatment. Stable two-headed regeneration after a two-day treatment, reversible without a genetic change, would support multiple stored targets; immediate reversion after washout, or a mutation that co-segregates with head number, would refute it.
obstacles: Persistent drug, epigenetic marks, or microbiome changes can store the phenotype without a bioelectric target representation.
Head-number counts are in the experimental papers, not in a public individual-level file, and the lines have not been shown by a deposited genome to be free of mutations.
assessments.rationale: The memory operationalization is the right kind: a persistent change in regenerative outcome after a transient stimulus, with a reset. Published planarian experiments report that pattern for wild-type stocks. Those counts are not a reusable dataset, and several non-bioelectric stores fit the same persistence, so existing reports test the phenomenon only in part.

assessments.operationalization: Quantify head outlines of gap-junction-blocker-treated genetically wild-type Girardia dorotocephala and compute morphological distances to untreated heads of other planarian species, then place those species on a dated phylogeny. Treated heads falling nearer other species' shapes than their own controls, across divergence times on the order of 100 to 150 million years, would support the report; shapes that are only disrupted, or divergence times far from that range for the species actually compared, would count against the corresponding clause.

candidate_datasets.name: TimeTree
candidate_datasets.role: dated divergences among planarian lineages for the 100–150 million year clause; it does not contain the head outlines

obstacles: Head-shape measurements live in the 2015 paper's figures, not in TimeTree or a morphometric archive.
A generic dysmorphic head can be scored as species-like unless the distance to each species shape is pre-specified.
assessments.rationale: Shape distance and divergence time are both measurable, and TimeTree can check the temporal clause once the species pair is fixed. The shape data are the published images from one experiment, not an open landmark file, so an independent remasurement is limited. Species-specific recapitulation has to be separated from nonspecific disruption.

assessments.operationalization: Track ciliary beat direction and feeding after a 180-degree cortical rotation in Paramecium or a related ciliate, across asexual generations, and sequence the same lines. Inheritance of reversed beating with a genome that matches the unoperated stock would support cortical inheritance that the genome does not correct; loss of the reversal within a few fissions, or a fixed nuclear mutation, would refute it.

candidate_datasets.name: Ciliate Genome Database
candidate_datasets.role: reference genomes for Paramecium and Tetrahymena; it does not include the surgically rotated lines

obstacles: The classical lines were not sequenced, so wild-type DNA is inferred from genetics rather than from a public genome of those cells.
The primary observations are journal descriptions from the 1960s onward, not a single downloadable pedigree.
assessments.rationale: Cortical rotation, inheritance across fissions, and failure of the nucleus to restore normal feeding are concrete and were reported repeatedly in the ciliate literature. Reference genomes exist, but not for the operated lines, so the wild-type-DNA clause cannot be rechecked from sequence. The anatomical inheritance can be assessed from the published experiments, with the limits of pre-genomic records.

assessments.operationalization: Reanalyze the Dugesia japonica barium RNA-seq with a pre-specified handful rule, for example fewer than 20 genes at FDR under 0.05 and a stated fold change, in heads that regenerated in BaCl2 versus controls. A count under that cutoff would support the transcriptional clause; a count of dozens or hundreds would refute a handful.

candidate_datasets.name: GEO series GSE98084
candidate_datasets.role: public RNA-seq of Dugesia japonica adapting to barium chloride, for a recount of differentially expressed genes

obstacles: A handful is undefined until a threshold is fixed, and the original paper used a stringent fold-change cutoff.
Pooled or few samples limit the stability of the gene list, and the anatomical time course is not in the expression matrix.
assessments.rationale: The expression half is directly in a public series and can be recounted with ordinary differential-expression methods. That recount can support or refute a small gene list, which is only part of the statement. Head loss and barium-insensitive regrowth, and the reading that cells thereby solved an unselected problem, are not variables in the count matrix and are not discriminated from a generic stress transcriptome.

assessments.operationalization: Rank species by an explicit regeneration score, a cancer-incidence measure, and a longevity measure, then test whether high regeneration predicts low cancer and long life after phylogenetic correction. A joint association in that direction would support the comparative pattern; regenerative taxa with high cancer or short life, or a pattern that vanishes under phylogeny and body size, would count against it.

candidate_datasets.name: AnAge
candidate_datasets.role: species longevity records for the aging clause; it does not score regeneration or cancer

obstacles: Regeneration ability and comparative cancer rates are not in one open table and are biased by how hard tumors are to see in small aquatic animals.
Body size, phylogeny, and indeterminate growth confound any three-way association.
assessments.rationale: Longevity is tabulated for many species, so the aging arm has a real dataset, while regeneration and cancer resistance are scattered qualitative reports. A phylogenetically controlled test can be sketched for a subset of taxa and would be informative only with serious confounds. The expectation about undifferentiated cells and cancer is not a separate measured variable.

assessments.operationalization: In the public competency model, track the fraction of fitness-improving changes that alter competency parameters versus structural genes as competency is allowed to evolve. An increasing share of competency edits, and weaker selection on the structural genome, would support the ratchet inside that model; continued improvement mainly in structural genes would refute it there.

candidate_datasets.name: Cellular competency evolution model
candidate_datasets.role: public code and pre-saved runs for hardwired, competent, and evolvable-competency populations

obstacles: The model uses a one-dimensional positional target, so its ratchet need not be the biological one.
Ordering planaria, salamanders, and mammals by degree of competency is not a variable in the saved runs.
assessments.rationale: The computational ratchet is re-runnable from a public repository that already stores simulation outputs, so that part can be confirmed or refuted by a standard reanalysis. The claim also ranks real lineages, and nothing in the repository or in a comparable open table measures their competency. The model result is a proxy for the evolutionary statement, not the whole of it.

assessments.operationalization: Search FlyBase, Mouse Genome Informatics, and the planarian literature for stable inherited strains whose anatomy differs from wild type in the absence of ongoing RNAi or drug treatment. Morphological mutant strains in flies and mice, and at least one published planarian strain of that kind, would refute the negative planarian clause; a documented absence of such planarian strains, with the only permanent abnormal lines being the bioelectric one-head and two-head forms, would support it as a statement about the public record.

candidate_datasets.name: FlyBase
candidate_datasets.role: catalog of Drosophila strains with abnormal morphology, the contrast class

candidate_datasets.name: Mouse Genome Informatics
candidate_datasets.role: catalog of mouse mutant alleles and phenotypes, the other contrast class

candidate_datasets.name: PubMed
candidate_datasets.role: index of planarian genetics papers through which a stable morphological mutant strain would be found

obstacles: RNAi phenotypes and transient drug phenotypes are easy to mistake for mutant strains.
A literature search can refute the negative claim by finding a strain, but cannot prove that no unpublished strain exists.
Transgenesis attempts after the paper's publication can change the public record without a single dedicated database.
assessments.rationale: The contrast with flies and mice is directly queryable in phenotype databases, and planarian strain reports are public literature. That is enough to test a claim about what is known, including the bioelectric origin of the familiar two-headed lines. It is not a complete census of stocks, and the competency-ratchet explanation of the absence is not tested by the search.

assessments.operationalization: From the saved competent and hardwired populations, compare phenotypic variance among genotypes, escapes from local fitness plateaus, and whether a deleterious local displacement is corrected before fitness is scored. Lower phenotypic differences and more escapes under competency would support smoothing and more efficient search in the model; identical landscapes would refute it there.

candidate_datasets.name: Cellular competency evolution model
candidate_datasets.role: public runs comparing evolvability of competent and hardwired embryos on a simple axial target

obstacles: The fitness landscape is a toy monotonic gradient, so local maxima of real development are not in the data.
Smoothing by competency is not separated, in organisms, from canalization by other mechanisms.
assessments.rationale: The model was built to compare hardwired and regulative development and its outputs are public, so the efficiency and masking effects can be recomputed. That tests the mechanism inside the stated simulation, which covers only a thin analogue of regulative evolution. Organismal fitness landscapes and the hypothetical mouth correction are not in those files.

assessments.operationalization: Estimate the fraction of mutations that are phenotypically silent under normal development and revealed under a perturbation, in a system with regulative development, and compare with a direct genotype-to-phenotype encoding if one is available. A larger silent pool that later becomes visible would support cryptic variation produced by buffering; absence of that pool, or a pool explained by protein chaperones rather than developmental correction, would count against the competency-specific version.

candidate_datasets.name: FlyBase
candidate_datasets.role: alleles and phenotype annotations for Drosophila cryptic-variation and capacitor experiments, a partial biological analogue

candidate_datasets.name: Cellular competency evolution model
candidate_datasets.role: public comparison of how developmental correction hides structural-gene differences from selection

obstacles: Cryptic variation is well documented for chaperones and redundancy, which are rivals to multiscale competency.
FlyBase does not record a pool of mutations buffered specifically by anatomical error correction.
assessments.rationale: Cryptic genetic variation can be surveyed in Drosophila resources, and the competency model can show mutations hidden from selection by a developmental layer. Those are partial proxies. They do not identify multiscale competency, as opposed to other buffering, as the cause of a dormant pool that evolution later exploits.

assessments.operationalization: Measure habituation as reduced crossing of a noxious region after repeated exposure, recovered by a dishabituation control, and measure growth direction toward inert objects that differ in mass. Reduced withdrawal plus reliable growth toward the heavier object would support the learning and decision results; no change, or growth explained by a chemical cue correlated with mass, would count against them.
obstacles: Raw trajectories are spread across papers and video supplements, not one archive.
Habituation protocols differ, and some replications have been disputed.
Growth toward mass can be a biomechanical taxis without a decision variable.
assessments.rationale: Habituation and growth direction are standard measurements, and several independent Physarum papers report them, so a restricted test can be assembled from published results. There is no single open trajectory archive, and the mass result in particular needs its controls rechecked from the source paper. The identification of behaviour with morphological change is true of this organism's mode of movement and does not further discriminate the learning result.

assessments.operationalization: Train intact planarians on a specified task, cut off tails, let the tails regenerate a brain, and compare task performance with naive regenerated controls and with animals trained after regeneration. Retention above both controls would support memory in the new brain; performance explained by residual tissue, sensitization, or experimenter cueing would refute it.
obstacles: McConnell's mid-century protocols are widely regarded as poorly controlled, and raw trial sheets are not public.
The modern Dugesia japonica result is one laboratory's published summary, without a deposited trial table.
assessments.rationale: Retention after regeneration is a clear behavioural contrast, and two published studies report it. Their measurements can be reassessed only at the level of published summaries, and the older study is confounded. Existing reports therefore test the phenomenon partially and do not settle whether the new brain received an imprint of the original training.

assessments.operationalization: In Xenopus tadpoles with no primary eyes and one tail eye, score visually guided learning and trace axons from that eye. Learning that requires the tail eye, with axons entering the spinal cord, would support seeing through the ectopic eye; chance performance, or learning that remains after the tail eye is removed, would refute it.
obstacles: Published performance is a summary, not trial-level choices.
Extraocular photoreception is the main rival and has to be read off the paper's controls.
assessments.rationale: This is the same preparation as the behavioural tail-eye result, with a narrower endpoint: vision and a spinal connection. The experimental paper publishes those outcomes for this scope. They can be checked against the described controls and cannot be recomputed from an open trial file.

assessments.operationalization: In paired transcriptome and electrophysiology profiles, predict resting or firing features from transcript levels and ask whether distinct channel sets map to the same electrical phenotype. Prediction no better than a permutation null, or identical transcriptomes with different voltage states, would support unreadability; accurate prediction of the electrical phenotype from transcripts or proteins would refute a strict reading.

candidate_datasets.name: Allen Brain Cell Types
candidate_datasets.role: public patch-seq and electrophysiology for mammalian cortical neurons, pairing transcripts with electrical features
